NOV 2 - 1939

Jury Gives Verdict Of
Not Guilty In Morris
“Manslaughter” Trial

Case Of Crown vs. J. D. Morris Ends When Judge
Acquits Accused After Jury’s Verdict Is
Announced; Morris Is Freed

JUDGE GIVES JURY FOUR QUESTIONS
TO ANSWER TO REACH DECISION

After considering the evidence of both sides for 35 minutes, the five members of the jury returned to the courtroom of H.B.M. Supreme Court yesterday evening and gave a verdict of “Not Guilty” in the case of the Crown versus John Dudley Morris, an inspector of the Public Health Department who was charged with the manslaughter of Ting Shu-cheng, a Chinese brothel-keeper on the night of September 8, last.

The case lasted another full day yesterday, finally ending at 5.40 p.m. when the jurymen filed back into their seats and gave the Judge their decision. The Judge, Sir Allan Mossop, thereupon said, “John Dudley Morris you are discharged,” and the former prisoner left the dock, automatically becoming a completely free man again.

The Judge facilitated the task of the jury considerably by giving them a list of questions which they were to ask themselves about the accused. If they answered any one of the questions, which were to be taken in order, in the favour of the accused, he would not be guilty of manslaughter. The questions were:—
1.—“Did the accused strike the deceased?”
2.—“Did the accused cause or accelerate the death of the deceased?”
3.—“Was the accused who struck the blows, doing so in self-defence?”
4.—“Did the accused, when he struck the said blows, use more force than was necessary in self-defence?”

Judge’s Comments
By answering one of these questions in favour of the accused, the verdict would have to be “Not Guilty” and the charge against the prisoner dismissed. The Judge gave the jurymen certain advice before they retired to consider the verdict. He told them that “as regards the facts of the case, that is for you to decide. You are the sole arbiters of the case, and I am only here to direct you on the questions of law. But there is one thing which I must remind you about. It is the onus of proof. The onus of proof is always on the Crown, and never shifts to the accused. No matter what the charge, the principal for the prosecution must prove beyond all reasonable doubt that the accused is guilty of the charge. If you are left in any reasonable doubt, then you have to give the accused the benefit of that doubt.”

The Judge had also previously weighed up the evidence for the prosecution and that for the defence, and informed the jury of certain legal points concerning manslaughter charges. He warned them that the use of force was lawful when used in self-defence, but that no man had the right to shorten, even by an hour, the life of another.

1939年11月2日

陪审团在莫里斯“过失杀人”案审判中作出无罪裁决

随着法官在陪审团宣布裁决后宣告被告无罪，王室诉 J. D. 莫里斯案终结；莫里斯获释

法官向陪审团提出四个问题以供回答并作出决定

昨晚，英国陛下最高法院的五名陪审员在审议双方证据35分钟后返回法庭，就王室诉公共卫生局督察约翰·达德利·莫里斯（John Dudley Morris）一案作出“无罪”裁决。莫里斯被控于去年9月8日晚过失杀害中国妓院老板丁树成（Ting Shu-cheng）。

该案昨天又持续了一整天，最终于下午5时40分结束，当时陪审员们回到座位并向法官提交了他们的决定。法官艾伦·莫索普爵士（Sir Allan Mossop）随即说道：“约翰·达德利·莫里斯，你被释放了。”前被告随即离开被告席，自动重新成为一名完全自由的人。

法官通过向陪审团提供一份他们需针对被告自问的问题清单，大大便利了陪审团的工作。如果他们按顺序对其中任何一个问题作出有利于被告的回答，他就不构成过失杀人罪。问题如下：—
1.—“被告是否击打了死者？”
2.—“被告是否导致或加速了死者的死亡？”
3.—“实施击打的被告是否是出于自卫？”
4.—“被告在实施上述击打时，所使用的武力是否超过了自卫所需的必要限度？”

法官评语
只要对其中一个问题作出有利于被告的回答，裁决就必须是“无罪”，并对囚犯的指控予以撤销。在陪审团退庭审议裁决之前，法官给予了他们某些建议。他告诉他们，“关于案件的事实，由你们来决定。你们是案件的唯一仲裁者，我在此仅就法律问题向你们提供指导。但有一件事我必须提醒你们。那就是举证责任。举证责任始终在于王室（控方），而绝不会转移给被告。无论指控为何，控方主要代理人必须排除一切合理怀疑地证明被告犯有被指控的罪行。如果你们存有任何合理怀疑，那么你们必须给予被告该怀疑带来的利益。”

法官此前还权衡了控方和辩方的证据，并告知陪审团有关过失杀人指控的某些法律要点。他警告他们，在自卫时使用武力是合法的，但任何人无权缩短他人的生命，哪怕是一小时。

王室法律顾问约翰·麦克尼尔先生（Mr. John McNeill）和辩方律师 H. A. 里克斯先生（Mr. H. A. Reeks）在向陪审团总结各自案情时提出了论点。王室法律顾问对陪审员说，任何人心中都不可能存在合理怀疑，即丁确实是因一击而死。他说，莫里斯在其所有陈述中都承认击打了该男子，麦克尼尔先生主张死者是因被被告击打而死。
随后，麦克尼尔先生着手比较犹太难民马克斯·科普斯坦（Max Kopstein）和莫里斯证词中的某些要点。他说，他们的证词惊人地相似，科普斯坦的故事与被告的故事完全一样，只是后者在他的叙述中完全漏掉了前往贝加尔路（Baikal Road）74弄以及在该弄内发生的事件，而是从被告和其他两名同伴分道扬镳的那一点继续讲述。
他没有说在回家途中，三人均访问了74弄并进入68号房屋，然后从73弄出来到达韦赛德路（Wayside Road）并在此分手。麦克尼尔先生声称，被告在他的故事中遗漏了整个事件，并 stating 称在回家途中，当他们到达73弄入口时，他离开了另外两人，那两人走进了小巷。麦克尼尔先生请陪审团接受那些声称莫里斯在与其两位朋友访问68号房屋后，就在该房屋外击打死者的证人的故事。

辩方案情
代表辩方的 H. A. 里克斯先生在对陪审团讲话时说，如果他们相信被告是在科普斯坦的邀请下不情愿地返回现场去帮助陷入麻烦的李，并且是出于自卫而进行击打，他们就应当宣告他无罪。他指出，被告是来营救他的朋友，并且由于很快被敌对人群包围，他是出于自卫才进行击打。在这样的群体中，人们不会用尽全力出击，而仅仅是将攻击者挡开。
本案始于9月8-9日事件发生后不久在英国警察法庭进行的审理。在该法庭持续约一个月后，莫里斯被移送至高等法院，由法官和陪审团进行审判。昨天，许多此前在警察法庭作证的证人提供了证据并重述了他们的经历。上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）的卡明督察（Inspector Cumming）、警长克雷格（Detective Sergeant Craig）和迈耶警长（Sergeant Meyer）昨天都站在了证人席上，随后莫里斯也出庭作证。他重述了他在斗殴发生后约一小时告诉警长克雷格的故事，正如他当晚在警察局在卡明督察面前所作的书面陈述中所述，以及他在警察法庭在治安法官面前的陈述。

经辩方律师讯问后，莫里斯接受了麦克尼尔先生的交叉盘问。他问被告为何选择韦赛德路线回家。莫里斯回答说：“因为这对他们来说更近。”
“对你来说并不更近，是吗？”麦克尼尔先生问。
“不，但更方便，”被告回答道，并解释说贝加尔路和杨树浦路（Yangtzepoo Roads）的部分路段被日本人设置的障碍物堵塞。麦克尼尔先生试图通过提问证明莫里斯是经贝加尔路走另一条路线回家的，并且他与另外两人一起进入了74弄，后来在73弄入口处离开了他们。
莫里斯在交叉盘问期间还声称，中国证人和科普斯坦是被日本人授意编造了一套说辞，并举例说，科普斯坦被日本人只给米饭和水吃，直到他签署了由日本人 dictated 的供词。莫里斯还说，自己在华盛路（Whashing Road）海军办事处被迫签署了由日本人 dictated 的供词。卡明督察在其证词中证实了这一点。

NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS
1939
Briton Faces Manslaughter
Charge in H.M. Court
J. D. Morris Hears Prosecution Witnesses
Before Jury; Counsel Objects to Juryman
JOHN Dudley Morris, a 36 years old Briton employed at the
Chusan Road branch of the S.M.C. Public Health Dept., faced
a charge of manslaughter before a jury in H.M. Supreme Court
yesterday. Heard before Sir Allan Mossop, Chief Judge, the
trial of Morris followed a lengthy preliminary hearing in H.M.
Police Court in September when he was charged with the man-
slaughter of Song Kyung-dan, alias Ting Tszu-sung, whose death
had taken place, according to the prosecution, during a brawl in
a lane off Baikal Road in the early hours of September 9. As the
names of the jurymen were being announced by Mr. C. H. Haines,
H. M. Registrar, before the opening of the trial, an objection was
lodged by Mr. H. A. Reeks, on behalf of accused, to Mr. A. P.
Nazer, whose name was struck off. The five members of the jury
were: Messrs. J. Ward, L. E. Illingworth, H. C. F. Aris, S. S.
Sayer and H. Cadd.
In his opening, Mr. John McNeill,
the Crown Advocate, who prosecuted
on behalf of the Crown, outlined the
events leading up to the scene in
the alleyway where the Chinese had
died. He stated that the accused had
been detained by the Japanese Naval
Landing Party until 5 p.m. on the
following day, when he had been re-
leased and taken to a police station.
Kopstein, a German-Jewish refugee,
who was stated to have been with
Morris at the time, was also detained
by the Japanese Naval Landing Party,
and Lee, a Chinese, who was also
alleged to have been present, was
still under detention so far as he
knew.
The first witness to be called was
Torry William Robert Wilson, em-
ployed in the Land Office of the
Public Works Dept., S.M.C. He testi-
fied that plans (produced) had been
made under his supervision. Max
Kopstein, the next witness, told the
Court that at about 8 o'clock on the
evening of September 8 he was in
the Café Colibri, 18 Broadway, with
Lee, a Chinese employed by the
S.M.C. in the office of accused.
Visits to Cafes
Morris and a friend, whose name
he did not know, then entered and
sat with them at the table. After
having some beer they all left the
café at about 10.30 p.m. and proceed-
ed to Hongkew Police Station where
they had several drinks of beer in
the canteen. Leaving the canteen
when it closed, Morris, Lee and him-
self then went to the Café Carioca,
which was on Broadway, opposite
Wayside Post Office.
After drinking beer they left this
place at about midnight, walked along
Baikal Road and into a lane on the
right side. He could not remember
whether Morris or Lee opened a door
in the lane about 100 steps from the
entrance, but either Morris or Lee
opened the door of a house. All
three went a few steps inside the
house and at once walked back.

英国人在英国陛下最高法院面临过失杀人指控
J. D. 莫里斯在陪审团面前听取控方证人证言；律师对一名陪审员提出异议
36岁的英国人约翰·达德利·莫里斯（John Dudley Morris），受雇于上海公共租界工部局（S.M.C.）公共卫生局舟山路分局，昨天在英国陛下最高法院的陪审团面前面临过失杀人指控。由首席法官艾伦·莫索普爵士（Sir Allan Mossop）主持审理，莫里斯的审判继9月在英国陛下警察法庭进行的漫长预审之后进行，当时他被控过失杀害宋庆丹（Song Kyung-dan），又名丁子松（Ting Tszu-sung）。据控方称，其死亡发生在9月9日凌晨贝加尔路附近一条小巷的斗殴中。在庭审开始前，当英国陛下法院书记官 C. H. 海恩斯先生（Mr. C. H. Haines）宣读陪审员名单时，代表被告的 H. A. 里克斯先生对 A. P. 纳泽尔先生（Mr. A. P. Nazer）提出异议，其名字随后被划去。五名陪审员为：J. 沃德先生、L. E. 伊林沃思先生、H. C. F. 阿里斯先生、S. S. 塞耶先生和 H. 卡德先生。
在开场陈述中，代表王室起诉的王室法律顾问约翰·麦克尼尔先生概述了导致那名中国人死亡的小巷场景之前的事件。他指出，被告被日本海军陆战队拘留至次日下午5时，随后获释并被带往警察局。据称当时与莫里斯在一起的德裔犹太难民科普斯坦也被日本海军陆战队拘留，而据称也在场的中国人李，据他所知目前仍被拘留。
第一位被传唤的证人是托里·威廉·罗伯特·威尔逊（Torry William Robert Wilson），受雇于上海公共租界工部局工务局地政处。他作证说，（提交的）图纸是在他的监督下制作的。下一位证人马克斯·科普斯坦告诉法庭，9月8日晚上8点左右，他和受雇于上海公共租界工部局、在被告办公室工作的中国人李一起在百老汇路18号的蜂鸟咖啡馆（Café Colibri）。
光顾咖啡馆
随后，莫里斯和一位他不知姓名的朋友进入并与他们同桌坐下。喝了一些啤酒后，他们所有人于晚上10点30分左右离开咖啡馆，前往虹口警察局，并在食堂喝了几杯啤酒。食堂关门后，莫里斯、李和他本人随后前往位于百老汇路、韦赛德邮局对面的里约热内卢咖啡馆（Café Carioca）。
喝完啤酒后，他们于午夜左右离开此地，沿着贝加尔路行走，并进入右侧的一条弄堂。他不记得是莫里斯还是李打开了离入口约100步远的一扇门，但要么是莫里斯要么是李打开了一所房子的门。三人走进屋内几步，随即又走了回来。

证人走在前面，他以为莫里斯和李会跟在后面。当他转过身时，他看到莫里斯正在打一名中国人的嘴部。他不知道这名中国人是意外摔倒还是被击打的力量打倒，但他确实倒在了地上。他补充说，当他们进入房子时，他看到几名女孩，而他看到莫里斯击打的那名男子正在扫地。他没看到其他人。他说，这些女孩是妓女。

三到四次

科普斯坦称，他看到莫里斯击打该男子三到四次，击打时弄堂里有一名中国小贩。当该中国人倒在地上时，他们三人走出弄堂，回到贝加尔路，并进入马路对面的一条弄堂。然后他们朝贝加尔路方向走去。

在韦赛德路，莫里斯向他们道晚安，证人建议他和李走回那条弄堂看看那名中国人发生了什么事。当他们到达两条弄堂之间的贝加尔路时，几名中国人扑向李并开始殴打他。由于在场的中国人太多，他无法提供帮助，证人便沿着贝加尔路跑去寻求帮助。在斯塔德利大道（Studley Avenue）和贝加尔路的拐角处，他看到了莫里斯，并告诉他李正遭到袭击。

莫里斯不情愿地前往，在74弄入口处推开中国人，说道：“住手。”随后，中国人抓住了他和证人的手。上海公共租界工部局警务处的外籍63号警长随后赶到现场，科普斯坦继续说道，并询问发生了什么事。他让证人去韦赛德警察局。当时在场的还有另一名随警长前来的年轻人和几名日本人。他继续说，警长随后离开了。

他说，对话发生在躺着那名中国人的弄堂入口处，警长离开后，一些日本人来到现场，他们向弄堂深处走去查看尸体，尸体并未躺在确切的倒地地点，而是在对面。随后，多名日本海军陆战队员、军官和警察与他们三人一起进入一所中国房屋，并在那里待了一整夜。9月9日中午，他们被押送至宪兵队营房。

Previous Statements

Cross-examined by Mr. Reeks.
Kopstein said he worked in the Jew-
ish Refugee Camp on Ward Road and
during the course of the past few
months had worked with Morris. He
stated that he had never been to a
brothel with Morris. Mr. Reeks then
drew Kopstein's attention to a state-
ment he had made in the Police
Court as follows: "We turned right
into a lane. I do not know which
lane or number, I cannot remember
exactly what happened there as we
were drunk."

"Is that statement correct?" asked
Mr. Reeks. "I cannot remember ex-
actly what happened or followed as
we were drunk and I gave evidence
as far as I knew," Kopstein replied.
The Chinese, he added, was hit by
Morris three or four times. When
they had been in the café they had
not decided to go to a brothel and
nobody had said anything to him
about going to one of these places.
Asked why he had turned away from
his home to enter the lane, he said he
had merely followed the others. Mr.
Reeks then questioned Kopstein about
a statement which, he said, had been
made by witness in his office after
he had been asked if Morris had
been with him when he went to the
brothel, as follows: "I can't remem-
ber. My memory is a blank." In
Court Kopstein stated that he had
said this as he did not want to state
anything about the affair. Everybody
was asking questions, he said, he had
already given a statement to Inspec-
tor Cumming. "You replied to me,"
said Kopstein to Mr. Reeks, "we
will see one another again."

Rice and Water

"Was it not a condition of your
release," asked Mr. Reeks, "that you
made a statement" "I was told that
if I could remember I could go home
at once," replied witness. "Before I
met Inspector Cumming I was told
by a Japanese detective that I could
go home if I gave evidence." Wit-
ness said that he was released on
the 10th, and altered this to the 19th,
stating that he had made a mistake.
Upon being released he telephoned
Mr. Morris who had left two tele-
phone numbers. He met Morris, who
told him that he was facing a charge
of manslaughter and he was asked
to give evidence and to go and see
Mr. Reeks.
Mr. Reeks—Did you not tell Mor-
ris that you had been confined in a
room with fifteen Chinese and had
had foreign food only on one occa-
sion?—I never had foreign food. It
was always Chinese rice and water.
Mr. Reeks—Did you tell him that
you had been questioned daily and
that you had refused to make a
statement as you had no recollection
of the incident?—I did not want to
make a statement as I thought I could
get free without making a statement.

此前的陈述

由里克斯先生（Mr. Reeks）进行盘问。
科普斯坦（Kopstein）称，他在华德路（Ward Road）的犹太难民营工作，在过去几个月里曾与莫里斯（Morris）共事。他声称自己从未与莫里斯去过妓院。随后，里克斯先生提请科普斯坦注意他在警察法庭所作的一项陈述，内容如下：“我们向右拐进一条弄堂。我不知道是哪条弄堂或几号，因为我喝醉了，记不清那里究竟发生了什么。”

“该陈述是否属实？”里克斯先生问道。“因为我喝醉了，我记不清究竟发生了什么或后续情况，我只是就我所知提供了证词，”科普斯坦回答道。他补充说，那名中国人被莫里斯打了三四下。他们在咖啡馆时，并未决定去妓院，也没有人对他提起要去此类场所。当被问及为何离开自家方向而进入弄堂时，他说他只是跟随其他人。随后，里克斯先生就一项陈述向科普斯坦提出质询，据称这是证人在其办公室所作的陈述，当时有人问他莫里斯是否在他去妓院时与他同行，他的回答如下：“我不记得了。我的记忆一片空白。”在法庭上，科普斯坦称他之所以这样说，是因为他不想就该事件发表任何言论。他说，当时每个人都在提问，而他已向卡明督察（Inspector Cumming）作了陈述。科普斯坦对里克斯先生说：“你回答我说，‘我们会再见面的’。”

米饭与水

“获释的条件难道不是你作一份陈述吗？”里克斯先生问道。“有人告诉我，如果我能回忆起来，我可以立刻回家，”证人回答道。“在见到卡明督察之前，一名日本侦探告诉我，如果我提供证词，就可以回家。”证人称他是在10日获释的，随后又改为19日，并称自己搞错了。获释后，他致电莫里斯先生，后者留下了两个电话号码。他会见了莫里斯，莫里斯告诉他，他正面临过失杀人的指控，并要求他提供证词并去见里克斯先生。
里克斯先生——你难道没有告诉莫里斯，你曾被关在一个房间里，里面有十五名中国人，而且只吃过一次外国食物吗？——我从未吃过外国食物。一直都是中国米饭和水。
里克斯先生——你难道没有告诉他，你每天都受到讯问，并且因为对事件没有记忆而拒绝作陈述吗？——我不想作陈述，因为我认为不作陈述也能获得自由。

“White is Black”
“Did you state that you asked again and again about your release and that you were told that you would be released if you made a statement?” said Mr. Reeks. “Did you tell Morris that they stood you opposite Lee, face to face, and then asked him questions, that you had been told the details of what had occurred day after day, that you said if anybody were told day after day for nine days that white is black and if any one were kept on rice and water for nine days then one would agree that white was black?” “Yes, I said that,” said Kopstein, “but I meant that even if I knew nothing I would have to give a statement in order to get free.”
Before his release, he stated, he was given a paper to sign which was translated by a Japanese that he would never come back to the gaol of the Japanese.
“It seems to be a futile promise when they take you there,” stated His Lordship.
Witness still stated that he could not remember clearly what happened after they had left the Café Carioca. When they had been alone in the Chinese house in the lane after the affair witness stated that Morris told him to say that they had gone along Wayside Road.

Doctor’s Evidence
In the afternoon Dr. E. G. Gauntlett gave evidence that there had been an abraded wound on the red margin of the dead man’s upper lip and some clot and a small wound beneath it in the mouth. The right side of the chest had been filled with blood which, after an examination, was seen to have come from a large aneurism or dilation of the aorta, the main artery of the body. The aneurism had been caused by an old standing disease of the walls of the artery. Almost invariably death in these cases occurred from rupture or internal hæmorrhage caused by a fall, a blow or sudden excitement or any strain such as lifting a weight or hurrying. It would have been impossible for the man to have lived more than one or two months, he said.
A nephew of the dead man said that Morris, another foreigner and a Chinese entered his uncle’s brothel and asked for girls. After seeing a girl the Chinese slapped his master’s face while the foreigner seized him by his dress. The Chinese then pushed his uncle to the back door and as witness was greatly frightened, he ran away to a small shop on Yangtzepoo Road.

“指白为黑”
“你是否说过，你一再询问关于释放你的事宜，并被告知如果你作陈述就会释放你？”里克斯先生说。“你是否告诉莫里斯，他们让你与李（Lee）面对面站着，然后向他提问，有人日复一日地告诉你事件的细节，你说如果任何人连续九天被告知白就是黑，并且任何人被以米饭和水维持九天，那么他就会同意白就是黑？”“是的，我说过这话，”科普斯坦说，“但我的意思是，即使我一无所知，为了获得自由，我也不得不作陈述。”
他称，在获释前，有人给他一份文件签署，由一名日本人翻译，内容是他永远不再回到日本的监狱。
“当他们把你带到那里时，这似乎是一个徒劳的承诺，”法官阁下说道。
证人仍然表示，他无法清楚记得离开里约热内卢咖啡馆（Café Carioca）后发生的事情。证人称，事发后，当他们单独在那条弄堂里的中国房子里时，莫里斯告诉他说，他们曾沿着韦赛德路（Wayside Road）走去。

医生证词
下午，E. G. 冈特利特博士（Dr. E. G. Gauntlett）作证称，死者上唇红缘处有一处擦伤，口腔内该处下方有一些血凝块和一处小伤口。右胸腔充满血液，经检查发现血液来自主动脉（人体主要动脉）的大动脉瘤或扩张。该动脉瘤是由动脉壁的陈旧性疾病引起的。他说，在这种情况下，死亡几乎 invariably 是由跌倒、打击、突然兴奋或任何诸如举重或匆忙等用力导致的破裂或内出血引起的。他说，此人不可能再活超过一两个月。
死者的侄子说，莫里斯、另一名外国人和一名中国人进入了他叔叔的妓院并要求找姑娘。在看了一名姑娘后，那名中国人扇了他主人的耳光，而那名外国人则抓住了他的衣服。随后，那名中国人将他叔叔推到后门，由于证人非常害怕，他逃到了杨树浦路（Yangtzepoo Road）上的一家小店。

Bargaining
Upon returning he saw his uncle
lying unconscious in the alleyway
while the foreigner and the Chinese
were walking towards Baikal Road
still in the alleyway. "I ran after
the men and got hold of the Jew,
who was the smaller of the two for-
eigners," witness said, "and then the
Japanese arrived." Later he was
taken away by the Japanese with the
three men.
During cross-examination Mr.
Reeks questioned the witness in Chi-
nese. He asked, through the inter-
preter, when attempting to prove
that the brothel was one of the chea-
per and poorer kind, "You cater for
very small prices do you not? It
is a poor place is it not?" His Lord-
ship then stated "Ask what the prices
are," Mr. Reeks replying "It is a
matter of bargaining. I was nailed
into one as I went there yesterday
morning."
The Crown Advocate—"Did you
bargain?"—"I did not."
After evidence had been given by
Wong Ah-san that Morris had beaten
the dead man, and Wei yu-sing, who
said that a foreigner, whom he could
not recognize had hit the brothel-
keeper, the case was adjourned until
10 a.m. today. Before the adjourn-
ment Mr. McNeill asked if the testi-
mony of a Chinese female witness,
given in the Police Court, could be
given at the next hearing as the
girl had left for Ningpo. His Lord-
ship pointed out that he would have
to prove that the girl was unable to
travel, was dead or had left China
before his request could be granted.
"It is no good showing me that
she has gone to 'Ningpo more far'
as they say," he concluded.

讨价还价
回来时，他看到叔叔昏迷不醒地躺在巷子里，而那名外国人和那名中国人仍走在巷子里，朝贝加尔路（Baikal Road）方向走去。“我追赶那些人，抓住了那个犹太人，他是两名外国人中较矮小的一个，”证人说，“随后日本人到达了。”后来，他与那三人一起被日本人带走。
在盘问期间，里克斯先生用中文向证人提问。他通过翻译问道，试图证明该妓院是较为廉价和低档的一类：“你们接待的是非常低价的客人，不是吗？那是一个贫穷的地方，不是吗？”法官阁下随后说道：“问问价格是多少，”里克斯先生回答说：“这是一个讨价还价的问题。昨天早上我去那里时，就被死死盯上了。”
公诉律师——“你讨价还价了吗？”——“我没有。”
在王阿三（Wong Ah-san）作证称莫里斯殴打了死者，以及魏玉兴（Wei yu-sing，音译）作证称一名他无法辨认的外国人殴打了妓院老板之后，案件休庭至今日上午10点。休庭前，麦克尼尔先生（Mr. McNeill）询问，鉴于该女孩已前往宁波，能否在下一次听证会上提供一名中国女性证人在警察法庭所作的证词。法官阁下指出，在他的请求获得批准之前，他必须证明该女孩无法旅行、已死亡或已离开中国。“向我展示她去了‘更远的宁波’（Ningpo more far），正如他们所说，是没有用的，”他总结道。

Morris Manslaughter Trial
Opens Before Jury

Public Health Department Employee Pleads Not
Guilty; Alleged To Have Punched Chinese
Brothelkeeper In Mouth Causing Death

The trial of Mr. John Dudley
Morris, employee of the Public
Health Department of the Shang-
hai Municipal Council, on a charge
of manslaughter, was opened be-
fore Judge Sir Allen Mossop and
a jury of five in the British
Supreme Court yesterday morning.
Morris pleaded "not guilty" to
the charge that he, on the morn-
ing of September 9, "unlawfully
killed Zong Hoong-pah, alias King
Sung-zah."
The manslaughter trial lasted the
whole day yesterday and will be
continued at 10 o'clock this morn-
ing. Six witnesses for the prosecu-
tion were called yesterday by Mr.
John McNeill, Crown Advocate,
who, at the opening of the trial,
outlined the case to Judge Mossop
and the jury. Mr. H. A. Reeks, of
the law firm of Ellis and Hays,
subjected the Crown witnesses to
a gruelling cross-examination, es-
pecially Mr. Max Kopstein, the
chief witness for the prosecution.
The following five were picked
to serve on the jury, Messrs. L.E.
Ellingsworth, S.A. Scyer, J. Ward,
H.C.F. Aris and H. Cadd.
While the Crown contends that
Morris struck the deceased brothel-
keeper several blows on the mouth,
as a result of which he died, the
defence was trying to prove through
cross-examination yesterday that
accused was some distance from
the scene of the alleged man-
slaughter when the victim was
struck.

Visited Cabarets

In his brief outline of the case,
Mr. John McNeill said that on the
evening of September 8, Mr. Max
Kopstein was drinking in the Cali-
bre Cafe on Broadway with Mr.
Li, who worked under Mr. Morris
at the P.H.D., when Morris came
in with a friend and joined them.
They had some beer and later
drove to the Hongkew Police
Station canteen and had some more
beer. When the canteen closed the
party proceeded to Broadway and
went into several cafes there. Then
only Morris, Kopstein and Li re-
mained in the party.
They left the Carioca Cafe on
Broadway after midnight and were
going home, the Crown Advocate
alleged. On passing Lane 74,
Baikal Road, they went up to
House 68. They rapped on the door
to gain admittance, which was
opened by the proprietor, "who
the Crown alleges, was unlawfully
killed," continued Mr. McNeill.

《上海泰晤士报》
2637C

莫里斯过失杀人案审判
在陪审团面前开庭

公共卫生部门雇员 plea 无罪；被指控拳击中国妓院老板嘴部致其死亡

上海公共租界工部局公共卫生部门雇员约翰·达德利·莫里斯（John Dudley Morris）先生的过失杀人案审判，于昨日上午在英国最高法院由艾伦·莫索普爵士（Sir Allen Mossop）法官和五名陪审员主持开庭。莫里斯对指控 pleaded “无罪”，指控称他在9月9日上午“非法杀害了宗洪巴（Zong Hoong-pah，音译），又名金松扎（King Sung-zah，音译）”。
过失杀人案的审判昨天持续了一整天，将于今天上午10点继续。公诉人约翰·麦克尼尔先生（Mr. John McNeill）昨天传唤了六名控方证人，他在审判开始时向莫索普法官和陪审团概述了案情。埃利斯和海斯律师事务所（Ellis and Hays）的H. A. 里克斯先生（Mr. H. A. Reeks）对控方证人进行了严厉的盘问，特别是控方主要证人马克斯·科普斯坦先生（Mr. Max Kopstein）。
以下五人被选入陪审团：L.E. 埃林斯沃思先生（Messrs. L.E. Ellingsworth）、S.A. 斯耶尔先生（S.A. Scyer）、J. 沃德先生（J. Ward）、H.C.F. 阿里斯先生（H.C.F. Aris）和H. 卡德先生（H. Cadd）。
虽然控方主张莫里斯对死者妓院老板的嘴部进行了多次打击，导致其死亡，但辩方昨天试图通过盘问证明，当受害者遭到打击时，被告距离所谓的过失杀人现场有一段距离。

光顾歌舞厅

在简要概述案情时，约翰·麦克尼尔先生说，9月8日晚，马克斯·科普斯坦先生正在百老汇路（Broadway）的卡利布雷咖啡馆（Calibre Cafe）饮酒，与他在一起的是在公共卫生部门（P.H.D.）莫里斯手下工作的李先生（Mr. Li），这时莫里斯带着一位朋友进来并与他们会合。他们喝了一些啤酒，随后驱车前往虹口警察局的食堂，又喝了一些啤酒。食堂关闭后，这群人前往百老汇路，并进入了那里的几家咖啡馆。随后，只剩下莫里斯、科普斯坦和李先生三人。
控方律师称，午夜过后，他们离开了百老汇路上的里约热内卢咖啡馆（Carioca Cafe），正准备回家。经过贝加尔路74弄时，他们来到了68号。他们敲门以求进入，门由老板打开，“控方称，此人被非法杀害，”麦克尼尔先生继续说道。

The Crown Advocate related that
a quarrel took place during which
the proprietor of the brothel was
allegedly pulled or pushed out of
the house, "and there and then it
is alleged, the accused struck the
proprietor a number of blows,
whereupon he fell to the ground."
This was witnessed by a number
of persons. Mr. McNeill continu-
ed. After the scuffle the trio went
off, the accused going in the
direction of his home, while the
other two returned for some
reason or other to Lane 74, and
when they got there they were
surrounded by crowds and at-
tacked and later arrested. Morris
was called back by Kopstein to
help Li and was also detained.
Chief Witness
The chief witness for the pro-
secution, whom Mr. Reeks stated
during the trial Morris had hoped
would be the chief defence witness,
was examined and cross-examined
at length. He was called after Mr.
T. W. R. Wilson, of the Public
Works Department, S.M.C., had
produced some plans of the scene
of the alleged killing.
Mr. Kopstein, a German-Jew,
gave evidence through an inter-
preter. He confirmed Mr. McNeill's
outline of the start of the evening
in various cafes and the drinking
of beer. Shortly after midnight, he
said, Morris, Li and he left the
Carioca Cafe on Broadway and
went into a lane on the right.
They walked about 100 steps and
then Li or Morris opened a door.
When the door was opened the
three of them went in, related the
witness, and then at once walked
back. The witness walked in front
and thought that Mr. Li and Mr.
Morris would follow.
"When I turned around," the
German-Jew stated dramatically, "I
saw Mr. Morris hitting a Chinese
on the mouth. I don't know whe-
ther the Chinese fell accidentally
or whether due to the force of the
blow." Continuing, he stated that
he saw several girls in the house
and that the man who was later
struck was sweeping the floor when
they went in. The girls, he thought,
were prostitutes.
Upon being asked how many
times Mr. Morris had struck the
Chinese, Kopstein replied, "I saw
the accused strike the Chinese three
or four times. I also saw a Chin-
ese hawker in the lane," he added.
Why He Went Back
"After the Chinese was struck
and fell to the ground, all the three
of us walked out of the lane back
to Baikal Road," continued the wit-
ness. "Then we walked through
the opposite lane towards Wayside
Road. When we reached Wayside
Road, Mr. Morris said "good night"
and then I said to Li that we had
better go back and see what hap-
pened to the Chinese, as perhaps
we could help him."
"We went back, whilst Mr. Mor-
ris went home. Several Chinese
had gathered on Baikal Road and
jumped on Li and and struck him,"
related Mr. Kopstein, "I saw that
I could not help as there were far
too many Chinese and so I ran
along Baikal Road looking for help.
I saw Mr. Morris at the corner of
Studley Avenue and Baikal Road
and I told him that Li was being
attacked and that I wanted his help,
he did not go back willingly, but
I repeated the request twice and
finally he came."
"When we reached the group
Morris yelled to the Chinese to stop
and they stopped, but held Morris
and Li by the hands," stated Kop-

公诉律师叙述道，期间发生了争吵，妓院老板据称被拉出或推出房子，“据称，就在那时，被告对老板进行了多次打击，随后他倒在地上。”许多人目睹了这一过程。麦克尼尔先生继续说道。斗殴之后，三人离开，被告朝他家的方向走去，而另外两人不知何故回到了74弄，当他们到达那里时，被人群包围并遭到攻击，随后被捕。莫里斯被科普斯坦叫回以帮助李先生，也被拘留。
主要证人
控方的主要证人，里克斯先生在审判期间称莫里斯曾希望他成为辩方的主要证人，接受了长时间的讯问和盘问。在工部局公共工程处的T. W. R. 威尔逊先生（Mr. T. W. R. Wilson）出示了一些所谓杀人现场的平面图之后，他被传唤出庭。
科普斯坦先生是一名德裔犹太人，通过翻译提供证词。他证实了麦克尼尔先生关于当晚在多家咖啡馆开始活动及饮用啤酒的概述。他说，午夜刚过，莫里斯、李先生和他离开了百老汇路上的里约热内卢咖啡馆，走进右边的一条弄堂。他们走了大约100步，然后李先生或莫里斯打开了一扇门。证人叙述道，门打开后，他们三人走了进去，随即又走了出来。证人走在前面，以为李先生和莫里斯先生会跟在后面。
“当我转过身时，”这位德裔犹太人戏剧性地陈述道，“我看到莫里斯先生正在打一名中国人的嘴部。我不知道这名中国人是意外摔倒，还是因为打击的力量所致。”他继续说道，他看到屋里有几名女孩，后来被打的那名男子在他们进去时正在扫地。他认为那些女孩是妓女。
当被问及莫里斯先生打了那名中国人多少次时，科普斯坦回答说：“我看到被告打了那名中国人三四次。我还看到弄堂里有一名中国小贩，”他补充道。
为何返回
“在那名中国人被打倒在地后，我们三人都走出了弄堂，回到贝加尔路，”证人继续说道。“然后我们穿过对面的弄堂，朝韦赛德路（Wayside Road）走去。当我们到达韦赛德路时，莫里斯先生说了‘晚安’，然后我对李先生说，我们最好回去看看那名中国人怎么样了，也许我们可以帮助他。”
“我们回去了，而莫里斯先生回了家。几名中国人聚集在贝加尔路上，扑向李先生并殴打他，”科普斯坦先生叙述道，“我看到我无法帮忙，因为中国人太多了，所以我沿着贝加尔路跑去寻求帮助。我在斯塔德利大道（Studley Avenue）和贝加尔路的拐角处看到了莫里斯先生，我告诉他李先生正遭到攻击，我需要他的帮助，他并不情愿回去，但我重复了两次请求，最后他来了。”
“当我们到达那群人那里时，莫里斯对中国人喊叫让他们停止，他们停下了，但抓住了莫里斯和李先生的手，”科普

Cross-Examination
In the course of the cross-ex-
amination by Mr. Recks, Kopstein
stated that he worked and lived at
the Ward Road Jewish Refugee
Camp and that for the last few
months he worked with Mr. Morris,
their work extending often into the
night, having to visit sick refugees.
He admitted that he had never been
to a brothel before with Morris.
Upon being pressed on the point
that in the preliminary hearing
in the Police Court he had stated
that he was drunk and could not
remember what had happened.
Kopstein replied that he was drunk,
but that he had stated that he could
not remember exactly what hap-
pened.
Kopstein was also questioned
closely on the fact that he was de-
tained by the Japanese until Sep-
tember 19, and that he was ques-
tioned daily and that he had told
Morris that "if a man is told daily
that white is black and kept on
rice and water, then he finally
comes to believe same." Kopstein
contended that he had made no
statement to the Japanese. It was
brought out in the course of the
trial that the Chinese, Li, is still
being detained by the Japanese
Naval Landing Party.
Afternoon Session
Continuing at 2 p.m., Mr. J. Mc-
Neill, for the crown, called three
Chinese witnesses, Zung Teh-zung,
Wang Ah-san and Wei Yue-sing,
besides Dr. E. G. Gauntlett, who
had witnessed the autopsy on the
body of the deceased. The Doctor
stated that the deceased might have
suffered a rupture of the aorta from
the mere excitement of the fight; in
any case the internal haemorrhage
was sufficient to kill him. Death,
said the Doctor, would occur within
five minutes after the rupture.
The second witness yesterday
afternoon, Zung Tuh-zung, the
nephew of the deceased brothel
owner, retold his story as given in
the Police Court. He said that he
had heard the visitors knock on the
door, which was opened by the
owner of the house. Then, because
there were no girls awake at the
time, 2 a.m., the Chinese member
of the party slapped the witness's
master. One girl was called down
by the proprietor, but the Chinese
said she was not good enough. The
foreigner and the Chinese then
pushed the owner out of the back
door into the lane, and the witness,
who was frightened, ran out into
Yangtzepoo Road. He returned a
little while later and saw the three
men walking out of the lane
towards Baikal Road. "I ran after
them and caught hold of the
smaller foreigner, then some Japan-
ese gendarmes came along and
would not let us go." They were
taken to the Japanese Naval Head-
quarters on Whangpoo Road.

斯坦（Stein）说：“随后一名外籍巡捕前来询问发生了什么事，并呼叫了上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）和日本警察。接着我们走进弄堂查看尸体，由于人群拥挤，我看不清楚，但尸体并未躺在弄堂的同一侧。”
对科普斯坦（Kopstein）的讯问以他讲述日本海军陆战队到达后，他、莫里斯（Morris）和李（Li）被带进一所房子并在那里待了一整夜而结束。
交叉质询
在雷克斯（Recks）先生的交叉质询过程中，科普斯坦表示，他在华德路犹太难民收容所工作并居住，在过去几个月里，他与莫里斯先生一起工作，他们的工作经常持续到深夜，因为需要探视生病的难民。他承认以前从未和莫里斯一起去过妓院。
当被追问关于他在警察法庭初步听证会上曾声称自己喝醉了且不记得发生过什么这一事实时，科普斯坦回答说他是喝醉了，但他当时说的是不能确切记得发生了什么。
科普斯坦还就他被日本人拘留至9月19日、每天受到审问以及他曾告诉莫里斯“如果一个人每天被告知白的是黑的，并且只给吃米饭和水，那么他最终也会相信这一点”这一事实受到了严密质询。科普斯坦坚称他没有向日本人做过任何陈述。在审判过程中查明，华人李（Li）目前仍被日本海军陆战队拘留。
下午庭审
下午2点继续开庭，代表控方的J.麦克尼尔（J. McNeill）先生传唤了三名华人证人：宗德宗（Zung Teh-zung）、王阿三（Wang Ah-san）和魏岳生（Wei Yue-sing），以及见证了死者尸检过程的E. G. 冈特利特（E. G. Gauntlett）医生。医生表示，死者可能仅因打斗时的激动而导致主动脉破裂；无论如何，内出血足以致命。医生说，破裂发生后五分钟内就会死亡。
昨天下午的第二位证人是已故妓院老板的侄子宗土宗（Zung Tuh-zung），他复述了在警察法庭所作的供词。他说他听到访客敲门，房门由房东打开。当时是凌晨2点，因为没有醒着的姑娘，这群人中的华人打了证人主人的耳光。老鸨叫下来一个姑娘，但那个华人说她不够好。随后，那名外国人和那个华人将房东从后门推入弄堂，受惊的证人跑到了杨树浦路（Yangtzepoo Road）。过了一会儿他返回，看见那三个男人走出弄堂朝贝加尔路（Baikal Road）方向走去。“我追上去抓住了那个较矮小的外国人，随后几名日本宪兵过来，不让我们离开。”他们被带到了黄浦路（Whangpoo Road）的日本海军司令部。

Cross-Examination
The witness was then cross-examined by Mr. H. A. Reeks, who asked him if it was possible that the two foreigners and the Chinese whom he had seen inside the house were not the same men as the trio he had chased in the lane. The witness, however, stated several times that he was certain that they were the same men. After asking the witness a few questions about the locality, which the witness agreed was dotted with many other brothels, Mr. Reeks said "I was hailed by one (girl) myself as I went down the lane yesterday morning."
The next witness was Wang Ah-san, of House 56. Lane 74, Baikal Road. He reaffirmed his former evidence to the effect that he had left a house in the lane to buy noodles from a hawker in the alleyway, had eaten his noodles by the stall, and had then seen the fight. The owner, he stated, had been pushed out of his house by the two foreigners and a Chinese and beaten. One of them said, "We are from the S.M.C., and we will kill you in 10 minutes," the witness testified.
Both this witness and Zung Tuh-zung, the nephew of the brothel keeper, identified the accused as the foreigner who had struck the deceased. In cross-examination, the witness stated that there were only five people in the lane besides himself at the time of the fight. They were the two foreigners, the Chinese visitor, the proprietor and the stall-keeper.
Wei Yue-sing, the noodles-seller, told his story again. He had been selling his noodles and beef to a customer, the previous witness, he said, when the fight occurred: The deceased fell down on to the ground close to his stall, and the hawker had picked up his portable food stall and gone away.
During the questioning, Mr. Reeks found the interpreter's translation incomplete, on several occasions and so, with the permission of Judge Mossop, he questioned the Chinese witnesses in Chinese himself.
Mr. J. McNeill, for the crown, told the Judge that he had not been able to produce the female inmate of the brothel, Wang Siau-tsung, for she had been sent to Ningpo.
The Judge observed that this was against the counsel for the crown because as long as she was alive and in China she should have been produced. The law could not excuse her because she was in "Ningpo-more-far, as they say," the Judge declared.
The hearing was then adjourned until 10 o'clock this morning.

交叉质询
随后，H. A. 里克斯（H. A. Reeks）先生对证人进行了交叉质询，问他是否有可能他在屋内看到的两名外国人和那名华人，与他在弄堂里追赶的那三人并非同一群人。然而，证人多次表示他确信他们是同一群人。在问了证人几个关于该地区的问题——证人同意该地区散布着许多其他妓院——之后，里克斯先生说：“昨天早上我走下弄堂时，亲自被一名（妓女）招呼过。”
下一位证人是贝加尔路74弄56号的王阿三（Wang Ah-san）。他重申了之前的证词，大意是他离开弄堂里的一所房子，向巷子里的小贩买面条，在摊位旁吃完面条后，目睹了打斗。他说，房东被两名外国人和一名华人推出家门并遭到殴打。证人作证说，其中一人说：“我们是工部局（S.M.C.）的人，十分钟内就要你的命。”
这名证人和妓院老板的侄子宗土宗（Zung Tuh-zung）都指认被告就是殴打死者的那名外国人。在交叉质询中，证人表示，打斗发生时，弄堂里除了他自己只有五个人。他们是两名外国人、那名华人访客、房东和摊贩。
卖面条的小贩魏岳生（Wei Yue-sing）再次讲述了他的故事。他说，打斗发生时，他正在向前一位证人即顾客出售面条和牛肉：死者倒在他摊位附近的地面上，小贩收起他的流动食品摊离开了。
在质询期间，里克斯先生发现译员的翻译有几次不完整，因此，在获得莫索普（Mossop）法官的许可后，他亲自用中文讯问了华人证人。
代表控方的J.麦克尼尔先生告诉法官，他未能传唤妓院内的女性住客王小宗（Wang Siau-tsung）出庭，因为她已被送往宁波。
法官指出，这对控方律师不利，因为只要她还活着且在中国境内，就应该传唤她出庭。法官宣称，法律不能因为她身在“更远的宁波，正如他们所说”而予以宽免。
随后休庭，直至今天上午10点继续开庭。

驳斥此前一名证人关于他在9月8日晚前往贝加尔路74弄一家妓院的说法不实，上海公共租界工部局公共卫生处的英国雇员J. D. 莫里斯（J. D. Morris）先生昨日在英国警察法庭上，就导致一名华人在当晚死亡的事件提供了一个全新的版本，他因此被指控犯有过失杀人罪。
在莫里斯先生陈述了当晚发生的事件经过的听证会之后，书记官C. H. 海恩斯（C. H. Haines）先生将他移交高等法院审判。
莫里斯先生用缓慢而平稳的声音叙述了当晚的活动经过，他告诉法庭，9月9日凌晨约2点15分，他与德国难民马克斯·科普斯坦（Max Kopstein）先生以及工部局（S.M.C.）的华人雇员李先生一起，离开了东百老汇路（East Broadway）的一家名为“卡里奥卡”（Carioca）的咖啡馆，朝着他们各自住所的大致方向走去。
当三人从威赛德路（Wayside Road）入口到达贝加尔路73弄时，莫里斯先生为了摆脱同伴，在与他人道别后，继续沿威赛德路前行，绕道前往他在斯塔德利路（Studley Avenue）的住所。
科普斯坦求助
被告称，他刚快到家时，看见一名系着白领结的外国人追着他跑并呼喊警察。直到他到达自家后门，那名外国人才追上他，原来是气喘吁吁的科普斯坦先生。被告继续说道，双方互相认出后，科普斯坦先生抓住他的袖子喊道：“路上的一条弄堂里有人遇到麻烦了，莫里斯先生。你必须来帮忙。”
莫里斯先生抗拒拉扯袖子的行为，并正气凛然地回答：“如果在深夜这个时候有人遇到麻烦，干涉此事不是我的本分。我要回家。”
“是你的领班李（Lee）。”科普斯坦先生回答道，“弄堂里大约有50人，他们可能会杀了他。没有警察。你必须来，莫里斯先生。求你了，你必须来。”
被告随后让步，与科普斯坦先生一起跑向他现在知道是贝加尔路74号的那条弄堂。进入弄堂约30码处，大约二三十名华人正在斗殴，被告挤进人群中试图制止打斗并营救他的华**〔此处转录不清〕**

Morris Helps Friend
Mr. Morris saw Mr. Lee being attacked and struck by several Chinese whereupon he shouted to Mr. Lee to back away and put the flat of his hand on the chest of a man whom he assumed to be the ringleader. As he did this, another person whom he now recognized as the first witness, Zang Tuh-zang struck him behind the ear. A second Chinese on his left also struck him and the ringleader was in like manner aggressive.
After knocking witness Zang back against the lane wall. Mr. Morris warned the ringleader to cease his attacks. This policy did not work as the crowd continued to strike him, so after two more warnings Mr. Morris struck the ringleader three blows pulling his punches, however. At the third blow the ringleader collapsed into the arms of an adherent. Mr. Morris then shouted to Messrs. Kopstein and Lee to get out of the lane, his intent being to straighten out the matter of Mr Lee at Wayside Police station.

Trio Held By Mob
As the three approached the Baikal Road exit of the lane a Chinese shouted from the opposite end that one man was dead. They were then prevented from leaving by a crowd which had heard the shout. They walked back down the lane to where a Chinese lay stretched out on the pavement. They walked about in the lane for a few moments when two Japanese soldiers appeared and later a member of the S.M.P. in plainclothes who departed for Wayside Police station to get help. In a short time a Japanese naval landing party arrived on the scene and the three men were escorted to House No. 56 where a detective sergeant took a verbal statement from them.
The testimony of Mr. Morris was in almost complete contradiction to that of previous witnesses including Mr. Kopstein who declared the three friends had entered a brothel in Lane 74 Baikal Road and had subsequently gotten into a fight with the proprietor who fell before the fists of Mr. Morris.
With the preliminary hearings concluded and Mr. Morris committed for trial Mr. Haines permitted the accused liberty on a bail of $3,000 and two sureties of $3,000 each.

莫里斯帮助朋友
莫里斯先生看到李先生正遭到几名华人的攻击和殴打，于是他大声喊叫让李先生后退，并将手掌平放在他认为是带头闹事者的一名男子的胸口。当他这样做时，另一个他现在认出是第一位证人宗土章（Zang Tuh-zang）的人从背后击打他的耳朵。左边另一名华人也打了他，带头闹事者同样具有攻击性。
在将证人宗撞回弄堂墙壁后，莫里斯先生警告带头闹事者停止攻击。这一策略并未奏效，人群继续殴打他，因此在又发出两次警告后，莫里斯先生打了带头闹事者三拳，不过控制了力度。在第三拳打出后，带头闹事者瘫倒在一同伙的怀里。随后莫里斯先生大声呼喊科普斯坦先生和李先生离开弄堂，他的意图是去威赛德警察局解决李先生的问题。

三人被暴民扣留
当三人接近弄堂的贝加尔路出口时，一名华人从另一端喊道有一人死亡。听到喊声的人群随即阻止他们离开。他们走回弄堂，看到一名华人躺在路面上。他们在弄堂里徘徊了片刻，随后出现了两名日本士兵，后来又来了一名便衣的上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）成员，该成员前往威赛德警察局寻求援助。不久，一支日本海军陆战队抵达现场，这三名男子被护送到56号房屋，一名警佐在那里记录了他们的口头供词。
莫里斯先生的证词与此前包括科普斯坦先生在内的证人的证词几乎完全矛盾，科普斯坦声称这三位朋友进入了贝加尔路74弄的一家妓院，随后与房东发生争斗，房东倒在莫里斯先生的拳头之下。
随着初步听证结束且莫里斯被移交审判，海恩斯先生允许被告以3000美元保释金及两名各担保3000美元的保证人获得自由。

SEP 30 1939
25250

Briton Committed for Trial
On Manslaughter Charge

J. D. Morris Makes Long Statement After Charge
Is Framed in H. M. Police Court; Bail Increased

JOHN Dudley Morris, 36-year-old Briton employed at the Chusan Road branch of the Public Health Dept., S.M.C., was committed for trial on a charge of manslaughter yesterday by Mr. C. H. Haines, H.M. Registrar. Morris had been charged with the manslaughter of a Chinese named Song Kyung-dan, alias Ting Tszu-Zung, by the Shanghai Municipal Police, who alleged that the man had died as the result of being struck by Morris in a lane off Baikal Road on September 9. Present with accused during this affray, it was stated, were a German-Jewish refugee named Kopstein and a Chinese employee of the Public Health Dept. named Lee. Both of these had given evidence during the preliminary hearing.

At the opening of the hearing yesterday, Mr. G. H. Wright, for the prosecution, stated that his case was closed. Mr. Haines, addressing Morris, then stated "I have come to the conclusion that I must frame a charge of manslaughter. The charge is that you, John Dudley Morris at Shanghai on the 9th day of September, 1939, did unlawfully kill Song Kyung-dan, alias Ting Tszu-zung. Having heard the evidence do you wish to say anything to the charge?"

On behalf of Morris, Mr. H. A. Reeks replied that his client reserved his defence but he wished to make a statement from the dock. Morris then gave his statement as follows:

"At the first opportunity I made a free statement. That statement has been handed into Court and it is a true account of what occurred. It is absolutely untrue that I entered Lane 74, Baikal Road or any house in that lane in company with the witness Kopstein or the Chinese foreman, Lee.

"Between 2.15 and 2.30 a.m. on September 9 I left the Cafe Carioca in Broadway East in company with Kopstein and Lee. We proceeded along Wayside Road because that was in the direction of all our homes. I presumed Kopstein and Lee would proceed north on Chusan Road to their homes. My intention was to turn off Wayside Road into Lane 73 Baikal Road, which connects Wayside Road and Baikal Road. That would have been my nearest and normal way home.

"Screaming for Police"

"As we approached Lane 73, Baikal Road, on Wayside Road, Kopstein and Lee turned into Lane 73 Baikal Road instead of crossing the road and proceeding north on Chusan Road to their homes. Wishing to be rid of their company, I said goodbye without stopping and proceeded along the way home via Wayside Road, turning right into Macgregor Road past the Naval Landing Party Post, again turning right into Baikal Road, then proceeding towards my home in Studley Avenue.

"As I reached outside Lane 133 Baikal Road, I saw a foreigner in a white jacket some distance away, running towards me, screaming for police. By the time he reached me I was outside No. 127 Baikal Road or the rear entrance to my house. As he reached me he recognized me and I recognized him as Kopstein. He grabbed hold of my left coat sleeve, attempting to pull me along, and shouted 'Someone is in trouble in a lane along the road. Mr. Morris you must come and help.'

"I resisted his pulling and replied 'If anyone is in trouble at this time of night it is not my business to interfere. I am going home.' He still continued to pull me by my coat sleeve and shouted 'It is your foreman Lee. There are about 50 people fighting in the lane, and they might murder him. You must come Mr. Morris. Please you must come.'

No Intention of Fighting

"I gave way and ran with him to the lane. We ran into the lane, which I now know to be Lane 74, Baikal Road. Some distance inside the lane, about 30 yards, I observed a crowd of 20 to 30 Chinese blocking the lane. I pushed my way into the crowd with the intention of stopping the brawl in which my foreman was involved. I had no intention of fighting myself.

"In the centre of the crowd I saw foreman Lee being attacked and struck by several Chinese. I shouted to Lee to back away and put the flat of my left hand on the chest of a Chinese whom I assumed to be the ringleader, holding him back with the palm of my left hand. As I did this a Chinese, whom I now recognize as the first witness, Zung Teh-zung, struck me a heavy blow behind my right ear. Another Chinese on my left also struck me and the Chinese, whom I took to be the ring-leader, was striking at me from the front.

"I knocked Zung Teh-zung back against the wall of the lane, at the same time warning the ringleader to stop attacking me. I then pushed back the Chinese, who was hitting me from my left side, again warning the ringleader to stop fighting. He failed to do so, but continued to strike me on my right and left sides. I then felt others attacking me from behind, again warning the ringleader to stop. I warded off his blows with my forearms and as there was no sign of his ceasing, for self protection against the mob, I struck the ringleader three times, holding my punches, but sufficiently hard enough to prevent him further attacking me."

1939年9月30日
25250

英籍男子被交付审判
控以过失杀人罪

J. D. 莫里斯在指控确立后发表长篇陈述
于英国皇家警察法庭；保释金增加

约翰·达德利·莫里斯（John Dudley Morris），36岁，英籍人士，受雇于上海公共租界工部局公共卫生处舟山路分部，昨日由英国皇家书记官 C. H. 海恩斯先生（Mr. C. H. Haines）裁定就过失杀人指控交付审判。上海公共租界工部局警务处指控莫里斯过失杀害一名名为宋庆丹（Song Kyung-dan，又名丁子宗 Ting Tszu-Zung）的华人，警方称该人于9月9日在贝加尔路（Baikal Road）旁的一条弄堂内被莫里斯击打后死亡。据称，在此次冲突现场与被告人在一起的还有一名名为科普斯坦（Kopstein）的德裔犹太难民，以及一名名为李（Lee）的公共卫生处华籍雇员。这两人均在初步听证会上提供了证词。

在昨日听证会开始时，代表控方的 G. H. 赖特先生（Mr. G. H. Wright）表示其举证结束。随后，海恩斯先生对莫里斯说道：“我已得出结论，必须提出过失杀人指控。指控内容为：你，约翰·达德利·莫里斯，于1939年9月9日在上海，非法杀害了宋庆丹，又名丁子宗。在听取证据后，你对该指控有何陈述？”

代表莫里斯的 H. A. 里克斯先生（Mr. H. A. Reeks）回答说，他的当事人保留辩护权，但他希望从被告席上发表一项声明。莫里斯随即发表了如下声明：

“我在第一时间做了一份自愿陈述。该陈述已提交法庭，且是对所发生事件的真实记录。说我与证人科普斯坦或华籍工头李一同进入贝加尔路74弄或该弄堂内的任何房屋，这绝对不实。

“9月9日凌晨2点15分至2点30分之间，我与科普斯坦和李一起离开了位于百老汇路（东段）的卡里奥卡咖啡馆（Cafe Carioca）。我们沿着韦思德路（Wayside Road）前行，因为那是通往我们要去的各自住所的方向。我推测科普斯坦和李会沿舟山路向北回家。我的打算是从韦思德路转入贝加尔路73弄，该弄堂连接韦思德路和贝加尔路。那将是离我家最近且正常的回家路线。

‘呼喊警察’

“当我们在韦思德路上接近贝加尔路73弄时，科普斯坦和李转入了贝加尔路73弄，而不是穿过马路沿舟山路向北回家。为了摆脱他们的陪伴，我没有停下脚步便道别，然后继续沿韦思德路回家，经过海军登陆部队岗哨后右转进入麦格雷戈路（Macgregor Road），再次右转进入贝加尔路，随后朝我在斯塔德利大道（Studley Avenue）的住所走去。

“当我到达贝加尔路133弄外时，我看到远处有一名身穿白色夹克的外国人正朝我跑来，大声呼喊警察。当他跑到我身边时，我正处在贝加尔路127号外或我家后门处。他跑到我身边时认出了我，我也认出他是科普斯坦。他抓住我的左外套袖子，试图拉我走，并喊道：‘路上有条弄堂里有人出事了。莫里斯先生，你必须来帮忙。’

“我抗拒他的拉扯并回答道：‘如果在这个时间点有人出事，干涉并非我的本分。我要回家。’他仍然继续拉着我的外套袖子喊道：‘是你的工头李。弄堂里大约有50人在打架，他们可能会杀了他。你必须来，莫里斯先生。求求你，你必须来。’

无意斗殴

“我让步了，随他跑向那条弄堂。我们跑进弄堂，我现在知道那是贝加尔路74弄。进入弄堂约30码深处，我看到有二三十名华人堵住了弄堂。我挤进人群，意图制止卷入我工头的斗殴。我自己并无斗殴之意。

“在人群中央，我看到工头李正遭到几名华人的攻击和殴打。我大喊让李退后，并将左手掌平放在一名我认为是一伙人之首的华人胸前，用左手掌将其挡住。就在我这样做的时候，一名华人——我现在认出他是第一证人宗德宗（Zung Teh-zung）——重重地击打了我的右耳后方。我左侧的另一名华人也击打了我，而我认为是一伙人之首的那名华人则从正面攻击我。

“我将宗德宗撞向弄堂的墙壁，同时警告那为首者停止攻击我。随后，我将左侧击打我的那名华人推开，再次警告为首者停止打斗。他并未照做，而是继续从左右两侧击打我。接着我感到其他人从背后攻击我，我再次警告为首者停止。我用前臂挡开他的击打，由于他没有停止的迹象，为了在暴民面前自我保护，我击打了为首者三次，有所克制，但力度足以防止他进一步攻击我。”

Bail Increased

"As I struck him the third time he
fell back, not to the ground, but into
the arms of other Chinese standing
behind him. They immediately drag-
ged him away and all fighting ceased.
I then shouted to Kopstein and Lee
to get out of the lane, my intention
being to take Lee to Wayside Police
station where his dispute could be
settled. The three of us walked to-
gether towards the entrance without
interference.
"As we approached the lane en-
trance on Baikal Road a Chinese in
the southern part (Yangtszepoo end)
of the lane shouted 'One man is
dead.' We were prevented from
leaving the lane by : crowd of Chin-
ese at the Baikal Road entrance.
They had heard the shout of 'One
man is dead.' We walked back into
the lane for a distance of about 50
yards past the scene of the fight and
there saw a Chinese male whom I
previously presumed to be the ring-
leader, lying on the pavement of the
lane.
"We walked about in the lane for
a few moments and two Japanese
soldiers and a foreign Shanghai Muni-
cipal police officer in plain clothes
arrived simultaneously. We waited
there for a few minutes while the
foreign policeman went to Wayside
Police station for help. Shortly after-
wards the Japanese Naval Landing
Party arrived and placed us under
escort in House 56. A few minutes
later a detective-sergeant from Way-
side Police station arrived and took
verbal statements from Lee, Kop-
stein and myself."
Following a submission by Mr.
Wright that bail should be increased
while accused was awaiting trial, Mr.
Haines stated that he would increase
each of the three sureties by $1,000.
Defendant was then allowed bail on
his own recognizance of $3,000 and
two other sureties of $3,000 each.

SEP 29 1939

Morris To Face
Supreme Court

New Story Recounted
On Brothel Keeper
Manslaughter

Relating an account differing
from testimony previously made,
Mr. J. D. Morris, employee of the
SMC Public Health Department,
gave evidence this morning on his
own behalf at the conclusion of
preliminary hearings against him
on a charge of manslaughter in
the British Police Court, of the
events which led up to the death
of a Chinese brothel proprietor in
Wayside on September 9. Follow-
ing the defendant's evidence the
Magistrate, Mr. C. H. Haines com-
mitted Morris to trial by the Bri-
tish Supreme Court, bail being
fixed at $3000 and two sureties of
$3000.

According to his evidence in
court this morning, Morris stated
that he was in the Carioca Bar
until 2 a.m. on September 9, when
he left the place in the company
of a Chinese PHD foreman and
Max Kopstein, a German-Jewish
refugee employed for extra work
among refugees by the PHD.
Leaves Companions
Morris stated that he left the
two men at the corner of Balkal
Road and Studley Avenue, pro-
ceeding along the latter thorough-
fare to reach his home. After
walking for a few minutes he
heard someone running behind
him and then saw that it was
Kopstein. The latter, Morris said,
asked him to return with him and
help the foreman who was in-
volved in a fight with a large
crowd of Chinese. After hesitating,
Morris accompanied Kopstein and
then came upon a crowd of 20 or
30 Chinese who were fighting.
Continuing, Morris declared
that he shouted to the crowd to
stop fighting. Just then, Morris
stated, Sun Teh-zeng, one of the
earlier witnesses in the hearings,
came up from behind the defen-
dant and struck the latter on the
back. Morris turned around and
caught one of the Chinese, whom
he "hit several times."
The person whom he had struck,
Morris went on, did not fall to
the ground, but dropped into the
arms of another Chinese.

NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS.

SEP 26 1939

Final Stages Reached in
Manslaughter Case

Briton Hears Evidence of Fight Outside Brothel
Near Baikal Road ; Defence Counsel's Objections

THE final stages of the preliminary examination of John Dudley Morris, a 36-year-old Briton employed at the Chusan Road branch of the S.M.C. Public Health Dept., on a complaint of manslaughter, were reached in H.M. Police Court before Mr. C. H. Haines, Registrar, yesterday. Morris had been charged by the Shanghai Municipal Police with manslaughter following the death of a Chinese named Ting Shu-cheng, a brothel-keeper, following an alleged brawl outside his home early on the morning of September 9. It will be recalled that Morris and two other men, a German-Jewish refugee and a Chinese named Li, were detained by the Japanese military authorities for some time following the incident. The hearing was adjourned until 10 a.m. on Friday.

First witness to be called was Dr. Eric Gerald Gauntlett, a British registered medical practitioner, who said that on the morning of September 9, at the request of the Shanghai Municipal Police, he went with Det.-Sub Insp. Cunning of the S.M.P. to the Japanese Naval Landing Party Hospital in North Szechuen Road to witness an autopsy performed on the body of a male Chinese.

Det.-Sub-Insp. Cumming, said Dr. Gauntlett, had informed him that the Chinese was reported to have been assaulted during the night and had died in consequence. Two Japanese naval medical officers performed the autopsy, he continued, and he was given every opportunity to see the examination closely.

After referring to his report Dr. Gauntlett stated "The body appeared to be that of a medium-sized, middle-aged Chinese male. There was a bruise or abrasion on the red margin of the upper lip and some blood clot and a small wound on the centre of the gum, beneath it one, or possibly two, teeth were missing.

"The appearance of the lip and gum was consistent with a recent blow which had knocked out or broken two teeth. There was no sign of bleeding from the nose, ears or eyes and no evidence of injury to the head, trunk or limbs, except the injury to the mouth described above.

Liable to Sudden Death

"On opening the chest, the right side was found to be full of blood, which had come from a small rupture of a large aneurysm of the arch of the aorta, the main artery of the body. This aneurysm was caused by gradual weakening of the walls of the artery due to previous disease and would have been present for a long period, more than six months before death. Any person with such an aneurysm would always be liable to sudden death from rupture and internal haemorrhage caused by exertion or strain raising the blood pressure sufficiently to burst the already thinned and weakened wall and such a rupture is the natural termination of most cases of aneurysm in this position.

"In this case the exertion of taking part in a fight, the heavy impact on the ground, if knocked down, the sudden impact from a heavy blow in the mouth or even the excitement of a quarrel or an effort to defend himself may have been the determining factor in producing the rupture. From the large size of the aneurysm and the thinness of its walls, it is very unlikely that the deceased could have lived for more than a few months at the longest unless living as a complete invalid. The remainder of the organs appeared to be free from obvious disease."

Answering Mr. H. A. Reeks, for the defence, Dr. Gauntlett stated that Sub-Insp. Cumming did not tell him that accused had come to the scene of a quarrel and that an assault had ensued. He added "Inspector Cumming seemed to know very little about it at that time." After his evidence had been read over, he said the normal size of the aorta was from one to one and a half inches across while the dilatation was the size of two fists. It was the largest he had ever see...

Police Officer's Evidence

Mr. Torry William Robert Wilson, employed in the Land Office, P.W.D., identified two plans which had been made under his supervision at the request of the police. One showed the layout of Lane 74, which ran into Baikal and Yangtsepoo Roads, while the other was a key plan showing the roads in the district.

Det.-Sub-Insp. Cumming (recalled) said that the body of the Chinese lying in Lane 74, opposite House 68, was moved to the Japanese Naval Hospital, North Szechuen Road extension. Arrangements were made with the Japanese naval authorities for an English doctor to be present at the autopsy. Dr. Gauntlett was asked to attend and witness accompanied him to the hospital and back.

Prob.-Sergt. Eduard Meyer of the Shanghai Municipal Police said that in the early hours—between 2 a.m. and 3 a.m.—of September 9, he was east to west on Wayside Road. When he approached Lane 73, which ran between Baikal and Wayside Roads, he noticed a crowd of Chinese in the Baikal Road entrance.

He immediately proceeded to Baikal Road and in the entrance of Lane 74 he noticed about 20 to 30 Chinese, who were arguing and shouting. In order to see what was the matter he alighted and there he saw accused, whom he knew very well, standing in the middle of the crowd, being pulled about.

1939年9月26日

过失杀人案进入最后阶段

英国人听取贝加尔路附近妓院外斗殴的证词；辩护律师提出异议

昨日，在H.M. 警察法庭，由书记官 C. H. Haines 先生主持，对约翰·达德利·莫里斯（John Dudley Morris）过失杀人指控的预审进入了最后阶段。莫里斯是一名36岁的英国人，受雇于工部局公共卫生处舟山路分部。莫里斯被上海公共租界工部局警务处指控犯有过失杀人罪，起因是一名名叫丁树成（Ting Shu-cheng，音译）的中国妓院老板于9月9日凌晨在其住所外发生 alleged 斗殴后死亡。据悉，事发后，莫里斯与另外两名男子——一名德籍犹太难民和一名姓李的中国人——曾被日本军方当局拘留了一段时间。听证会休庭至周五上午10点。

第一位出庭作证的是埃里克·杰拉尔德·冈利特（Eric Gerald Gauntlett）医生，他是一名英国注册执业医师。他说，9月9日上午，应上海公共租界工部局警务处的请求，他与警务处副督察坎宁（Cunning）一同前往北四川路的日本海军陆战队医院，见证对一具中国男性尸体进行的尸检。

冈利特医生说，副督察坎宁告诉他，据报这名中国人在夜间遭到袭击并因此死亡。他继续说，两名日本海军军医进行了尸检，他获得了充分的机会近距离观察检查过程。

在提及他的报告后，冈利特医生陈述道：“尸体似乎属于一名中等身材的中年中国男性。上唇红缘处有瘀伤或擦伤，牙龈中心有一些血凝块和一处小伤口，其下方缺失了一颗，或者可能是两颗牙齿。

“嘴唇和牙龈的状况符合近期遭受击打导致两颗牙齿脱落或折断的情形。除上述口腔损伤外，没有鼻子、耳朵或眼睛出血的迹象，也没有头部、躯干或四肢受伤的证据。

易猝死

“打开胸腔后，发现右侧充满血液，血液来自主动脉弓大动脉瘤的一处小破裂，主动脉是身体的主要动脉。这种动脉瘤是由于先前疾病导致动脉壁逐渐 weakening 而形成的，且在死亡前很长一段时间（超过六个月）就已存在。任何患有此类动脉瘤的人，都始终面临因剧烈运动或用力导致血压升高，从而使已经变薄和脆弱的血管壁破裂并引发内出血而猝死的风险，而这种破裂是该位置大多数动脉瘤病例的自然结局。

“在这种情况下，参与斗殴的体力消耗、若被击倒则重重摔在地上的冲击、嘴部受到重击的突然冲击，甚至是争吵或自卫时的兴奋情绪，都可能是导致破裂的决定性因素。鉴于动脉瘤体积巨大且壁薄，死者除非完全作为病残者生活，否则极不可能存活超过几个月。其余器官似乎没有明显的疾病。”

回答辩护方 H. A. Reeks 先生的提问时，冈利特医生表示，副督察坎宁并未告诉他被告是来到争吵现场并随后发生了袭击。他补充说：“当时坎宁督察似乎对此知之甚少。”在他的证词被宣读后，他说主动脉的正常直径为一英寸到一英寸半，而扩张部分有两个拳头那么大。这是他所见过的最大的……

警官的证词

托里·威廉·罗伯特·威尔逊（Torry William Robert Wilson）先生，受雇于工务局地政处，指认了两份应警方要求在他监督下绘制的图纸。一份显示了通往贝加尔路（Baikal Road）和杨树浦路（Yangtsepoo Roads）的74弄的布局，另一份是显示该地区道路的索引图。

副督察坎宁（再次传唤）说，躺在74弄68号对面的那具中国尸体被移至北四川路延伸段的日本海军医院。已与日本海军当局安排一名英国医生在场见证尸检。冈利特医生受邀出席，证人陪同他往返医院。

上海公共租界工部局警务处代理巡长爱德华·迈耶（Eduard Meyer）说，9月9日凌晨2点至3点之间，他正沿韦思路（Wayside Road）由东向西行驶。当他接近位于贝加尔路和韦思路之间的73弄时，他注意到贝加尔路入口处有一群中国人。

他立即前往贝加尔路，在74弄入口处注意到大约20到30名中国人正在争吵和叫喊。为了看清是怎么回事，他下车，在那里他看到被告，他非常熟悉被告，站在人群中间，被人拉扯着。

25171

Japanese Soldiers Appear
Witness immediately went towards accused and asked him what was the matter when he also saw Mr. Kopstein, whom he knew as an assistant to Mr. Morris. After being questioned Morris told witness that he had been involved in a fight. All the Chinese at the time were shouting "He killed him." He then informed accused and others that they would have to go and investigate and they approached a Chinese lying in the middle of the alleyway about 100 yards from the entrance, his head pointing south and his feet north.
Prob.-Sergt. Meyer added that he told Morris that they would have to go to Wayside Police station but when they tried to leave they were prevented from doing so by two Japanese soldiers. Witness told them that he was a police officer but all efforts to get Mr. Morris and the other people to the station failed. He then told them to stay in the alleyway while he went to make a report.
After leaving the scene witness drove to Wayside Police station and, with two Japanese probationary sergeants and a Chinese detective, returned to the scene. Answering Mr. G. H. Wright, for the prosecution, witness stated that the body was near the back entrance of House 68. In answer to the cries of "He killed him," Morris told witness that he had hit the Chinese three times and he had collapsed.

Several Drinks
Max Kopstein, aged 20, whose evidence in German was translated by the previous witness, told the Registrar that he worked with Morris although he was not connected with the Public Health Dept. On the evening of September 8 he was in the Cafe Colibri, 18 Broadway, with a Mr. Li, who worked in the office of accused.
While they were there Morris came in and they had several drinks together. They stayed there until about 10 o'clock when Morris, and another Englishman whose name he did not know, Li and himself, went to Hongkew Police station to get drinks at the canteen. They stayed at the canteen until it closed.
From there they went by car to Broadway when they went inside a cafe. Here they had more drinks and from there they went to other cafes when the other Englishman left the party. Morris, Li and himself then left the Cafe Carioca, which was the last cafe visited, and walked along Baikal Road and turned right into a lane.
Answering Mr. Wright witness said that he could not remember exactly what happened as he was drunk. He believed that the Chinese showed Morris a door but he could not remember whether the Chinese or Morris opened it. All three went inside where they turned round once and walked out without anything happening. The place was a brothel, he said, and there were a few girls inside and he saw a Chinese, who was sweeping the floor. He did not know him.

日本士兵出现

证人立即走向被告，问他出了什么事，这时他也看到了科普斯坦（Kopstein）先生，他知道此人是莫里斯先生的助手。经过询问，莫里斯告诉证人他卷入了一场斗殴。当时所有中国人都在喊“他杀了他”。随后他告知被告和其他人他们必须去调查，他们走近一名躺在巷子中间、距离入口约100码处的中国人，头朝南，脚朝北。

代理巡长迈耶补充说，他告诉莫里斯他们必须去韦思路警察局，但当他们试图离开时，被两名日本士兵阻止。证人告诉他们他是一名警察官员，但将所有努力让莫里斯先生和其他人去警局的做法均告失败。随后他让他们待在巷子里，自己去报告。

离开现场后，证人驾车前往韦思路警察局，并与两名日本见习巡长和一名中国侦探返回现场。回答控方 G. H. Wright 先生的提问时，证人表示尸体靠近68号的后门。针对“他杀了他”的叫喊声，莫里斯告诉证人他打了那个中国人三次，后者便倒下了。

喝了几杯酒

马克斯·科普斯坦（Max Kopstein），20岁，其德语证词由前一位证人翻译，告诉书记官，他与莫里斯一起工作，尽管他不隶属于公共卫生处。9月8日晚，他与在被告办公室工作的李先生一起在百老汇路18号的蜂鸟咖啡馆（Cafe Colibri）。

当他们在那里时，莫里斯进来了，他们一起喝了几杯酒。他们一直待到大约10点钟，此时莫里斯、另一位他不知姓名的英国人、李先生和他自己，一起去虹口警察局在食堂喝酒。他们一直待在食堂直到关门。

从那里他们乘车前往百老汇路，进入一家咖啡馆。在这里他们又喝了一些酒，然后去了其他咖啡馆，期间那位英国人离开了这群人。随后，莫里斯、李先生和他自己离开了最后光顾的里约热内卢咖啡馆（Cafe Carioca），沿着贝加尔路行走，右转进入一条弄堂。

回答赖特先生的提问时，证人说他记不清确切发生了什么，因为他喝醉了。他认为那名中国人给莫里斯指了一扇门，但他不记得是中国人还是莫里斯打开的门。三人都进去了，在里面转了一圈，然后走了出来，没有发生任何事情。他说那地方是一家妓院，里面有几个女孩，他看到一个正在扫地的中国人。他不认识那个人。

25172

Chinese Said Struck

Witness added that he believed Li spoke to the Chinese although nobody touched him while they were inside. When they left the place witness went out first and waited for Morris and Li to follow. He turned around and saw Morris hit the Chinese, who had been sweeping the floor. Asked how many times Morris struck the man, witness said "Not more than five times." He did not know whether the man stumbled or was felled by a blow but he was lying on the ground. He added that he noticed a Chinese hawker and his stall but saw nobody else.

After the Chinese had fallen to the ground they walked away, crossed Baikal Road and went up the lane opposite until they got to Wayside Road. Here Morris said goodnight and added that he was going home. Witness then stated that he said to Li "Isn't it better that we go and see what has happened to the Chinese as he was bleeding from the mouth." This evidence was not taken by the Registrar and a protest was registered by Mr. Reeks.

Continuing his evidence witness said they went back to the same lane again as he thought they might be able to help the Chinese. They walked to the Baikal Road entrance but could not get any further because of a crowd of Chinese, one of whom jumped on Li and hit him. Seeing that Li was on the ground he went to get assistance and he saw Morris walking home near Studley Avenue and Baikal Road.

Detained All Night

Witness asked him to go along and help Li, who was being beaten by Chinese and he went back. On arrival at the scene Morris pushed the Chinese away from Li and the crowd then caught hold of Morris by the arm. Prob-Sergt. Meyer then came on the scene. Later two Japanese came with fixed bayonets and they walked towards the Chinese who was not lying in the same place but had been moved to nearly the opposite side.

Later about ten more Japanese arrived and they took witness, Morris and Li into a house in the same lane where they were kept in custody the whole night. Later they were marched to the Whashing Road Japanese military quarters where witness was detained all afternoon.

Mr. Reeks then asked witness if he had been to his office and had been asked one question "Did Morris go with you to the brothel or the lane where the brothel is?" Witness replied that the question had been asked and he agreed that he had answered "My memory is a blank. I do not remember whether he went with us or not."

Mr. Wright then stated that he would ask witness if he had made a statement substantiating what he had said in evidence. Mr. Reeks objected to this and the Registrar pointed out that if a witness had said something contrary to what he had said earlier in examination then the prosecution was entitled to refer him to an earlier statement.

Witness then said that before going to Mr. Reek's office he made a statement to Sub-Insp. Cumming which was read over to him and which he stated was correct. Mr. Reeks then asked for the statement to be produced and was stopped by the Registrar as he was about to question the witness. He again protested and asked that a note be made of the protest.

称中国人被打

证人补充说，他认为李先生同那个中国人说过话，虽然他们在里面时没有人碰他。当他们离开那个地方时，证人先出去，等着莫里斯和李先生跟出来。他转过身，看到莫里斯打了那个一直在扫地的中国人。当被问及莫里斯打了那人多少次时，证人说“不超过五次”。他不知道那人是绊倒了还是被一拳打倒的，但他躺在地上。他补充说，他注意到一个中国小贩和他的摊位，但没有看到其他人。

在那名中国人倒地后，他们走开了，穿过贝加尔路，走进对面的弄堂，直到到达韦思路。在这里，莫里斯说了晚安，并补充说他要回家了。证人随后陈述说，他对李先生说：“我们是不是最好回去看看那个中国人怎么样了，因为他嘴里在流血。”书记官未记录此证词，Reeks 先生提出了抗议。

证人继续作证说，他们又回到了同一条弄堂，因为他认为他们或许能帮助那个中国人。他们走到贝加尔路入口，但由于一群中国人而无法再前进，其中一人跳 onto 李先生并打了他。看到李先生倒在地上，他去寻求帮助，并在斯塔德利大道（Studley Avenue）和贝加尔路附近看到莫里斯正走回家。

整夜被拘

证人请他前去帮助正被中国人殴打李先生，他便回去了。到达现场后，莫里斯将中国人从李先生身边推开，随后人群抓住了莫里斯的手臂。接着代理巡长迈耶到达现场。后来两名带着刺刀的日本兵来了，他们走向那名中国人，那人已不在原来的位置，而是被移到了几乎对面的一侧。

后来又有大约十名日本兵到达，他们将证人、莫里斯和李先生带进同一条弄堂的一所房子里，他们在那里被拘禁了整整一夜。后来他们被押往华盛路（Whashing Road）日本军营，证人在那里被拘留了整个下午。

随后 Reeks 先生问证人是否去过他的办公室，并被问了一个问题：“莫里斯是和你一起去了妓院，还是去了妓院所在的弄堂？”证人回答说确实问了这个问题，并承认他回答的是：“我的记忆是一片空白。我不记得他是否和我们在一起。”

赖特先生随后表示，他将询问证人是否做过一份证实他在证词中所述内容的陈述。Reeks 先生对此提出反对，书记官指出，如果证人所说的内容与其在审讯早期所说的内容相矛盾，那么控方有权让他参考早期的陈述。

证人随后说，在去 Reeks 先生办公室之前，他曾向副督察坎宁做过一份陈述，该陈述向他宣读过，他表示该陈述是正确的。Reeks 先生随后要求出示该陈述，但在他准备询问证人时被书记官制止。他再次提出抗议，并要求将抗议记录在案。

SEP 26 1939
Important New Evidence
In The Morris Case
Dr. Gauntlett Says Deceased Could Not H...
Lived Longer Than A Few Months More;
Died Of Internal Haemorrhage

The fourth session of the case in which John Dudley Morris is appearing as the accused on a manslaughter complaint, continued yesterday morning in the British Police Court before the Registrar, Mr. C. H. Haines. The hearing lasted all morning, and during that time four new witnesses gave evidence and one other witness was recalled. The case was adjourned until Friday morning at 10 o'clock.

The first witness yesterday was Dr. Eric Gerald Gauntlett, local medical practitioner, who was requested by the S.M.P. to witness an autopsy on the body of the deceased. Detective Sub-Inspector D. A. Cumming of the S.M.P. escorted him to the Japanese Naval Landing Party Hospital, he said. "S.I. Cumming told me that a Chinese had been reported to have been assaulted and died in consequence," said the doctor. "The autopsy was performed by two Japanese naval medical officers, who gave me every opportunity of watching the examination closely. I prepared a report, but at present I have not submitted it to anyone."

Doctor's Opinion
Referring to his notes, Dr. Gauntlett gave his opinion as to the cause of death. He said that "the body appeared to be that of a medium-sized, middle-aged Chinese male. There was a bruise on the red margin of the upper lip and some blood clot and a wound on the centre of the gum beneath it, where one or possibly two teeth were missing. The appearance of the lip and gum was consistent with a recent blow which had knocked out or broken one or two teeth. There was no sign of bleeding from the nose, ears or eyes, and no evidence of injury to the head, trunk or limbs, except the injury to the mouth described above. Rigor mortis was present.

"On opening the chest, the right side was found to be full of blood, which had come from a small rupture of a large aneurism of the arch of the aorta, the main artery of the body. This aneurism was caused by gradual weakening of the walls of the artery due to previous disease, and would have been present for a long period, more than six months, before death.

Weakened Wall Of Aorta
"Any person with such an aneurism would always be liable to sudden death," Dr. Gauntlett declared, "from rupture and internal haemorrhage caused by exertion or strain, raising the blood pressure sufficiently to burst the already thinned and weakened wall. Such a rupture is the natural termination of most cases of aneurism in this position. In this case the exertion of taking part in a fight, the heavy impact on the ground if knocked down, the sudden jar from a heavy blow in the mouth or even the excitement of a quarrel or an effort to defend himself may have been the determining factor in producing the rupture.

Mr. H. A. Reeks, for the accused, questioned the witness who stated that "normally the size of the aorta would be an inch to an inch and a half across, while his dilatation was the size of two fists. It was the largest I have seen."

D.S.I. Cumming, of the S.M.P. was recalled, and he stated that the body of the deceased was removed from near House 68 in the lane to the Japanese Naval Hospital on North Szechuen Road extension. Arrangements were made for an English doctor to be present at the autopsy, and Dr. Gauntlett had been asked to go. He added that he had taken the doctor to the hospital and later brought him back.

Refugee's Story
Another witness was Max Kopstein, 20, a German Jewish refugee, who had been one of the three involved in the manslaughter of the brothel-keeper. Through an interpreter he told the Court that he worked with the accused, but was not in the Public Health Department. On the evening of September 8, he was in the Cafe Colibri on Broadway with Mr. Li, a Chinese who worked in the same office as the accused. While they were in this cafe, the accused came in and joined them. They had several drinks there and then some more in the canteen of the Hongkew Police Station. They had been joined by another Englishman. When the canteen closed they went by car to Broadway and had more drinks in several different cafes. The other Englishman left, and Morris, Li and the witness walked along Baikal Road.

"We entered a lane on the right," related the witness, who added that he could not remember exactly where the lane was because they were drunk. The Chinese Li pointed out a door, which someone opened and they all entered. "Nothing happened inside," the witness said, "and we turned around and walked out again. The place was a brothel and there were a few girls there. I saw a male Chinese who was sweeping the floor. No one touched him while we were in the house.

1939年9月26日
莫里斯案的重要新证据
高恩利特医生称死者不可能活……
超过几个月；死于内出血

约翰·达德利·莫里斯（John Dudley Morris）被控过失杀人一案的第四次庭审，昨日上午在英国巡捕房法庭由书记官 C. H. 海恩斯先生（Mr. C. H. Haines）主持继续审理。听证持续了整个上午，期间有四名新证人作证，另有一名证人被重新传唤。案件休庭至周五上午10点继续审理。

昨天的第一位证人是埃里克·杰拉尔德·高恩利特医生（Dr. Eric Gerald Gauntlett），他是一名本地执业医师，受上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）之邀见证对死者尸体的验尸过程。他说，警务处侦探副督察 D. A. 卡明（D. A. Cumming）陪同他前往日本海军陆战队医院。“卡明副督察告诉我，据报一名华人遭到殴打并因此死亡，”这位医生说。“验尸由两名日本海军军医进行，他们让我有机会密切观察检查过程。我撰写了一份报告，但目前尚未提交给任何人。”

医生的意见
高恩利特医生参照他的笔记，就死因发表了意见。他说，“尸体看似为一名中等身材的中年华籍男性。上唇红缘处有瘀伤，其下方的牙龈中心有一些血凝块和伤口，此处缺失了一颗或可能两颗牙齿。嘴唇和牙龈的状况符合近期遭受击打导致一颗或两颗牙齿脱落或折断的情形。除上述口腔损伤外，鼻、耳、眼均无出血迹象，头部、躯干或四肢也无受伤证据。尸僵已经出现。

“打开胸腔后，发现右侧充满血液，这些血液来自主动脉弓大动脉瘤的一处小破裂，主动脉是身体的主要动脉。该动脉瘤是由先前疾病导致的动脉壁逐渐 weakening（减弱）引起的，在死亡前已存在很长一段时间，超过六个月。

主动脉壁薄弱
“任何患有此类动脉瘤的人都随时可能突然死亡，”高恩利特医生宣称，“原因是用力或紧张导致血压升高，足以使已经变薄和弱化的血管壁破裂，从而引起破裂和内出血。这种破裂是该位置大多数动脉瘤病例的自然终结。在本案中，参与打斗的用力、被打倒时重重摔在地上的冲击、嘴部受到重击产生的突然震动，甚至是争吵或自卫时的激动情绪，都可能是导致破裂的决定性因素。

鉴于动脉瘤及其壁的薄度，我认为死者除非完全作为病残者生活，否则极不可能再存活超过几个月，最长也不过数月。其余器官似乎没有明显的疾病。”

被告方的律师 H. A. 里克斯先生（Mr. H. A. Reeks）对证人进行了质询，证人表示，“正常情况下主动脉的直径为一英寸到一英寸半，而他的扩张程度有两个拳头那么大。这是我见过的最大的。”

警务处的侦探副督察卡明被重新传唤，他表示死者的尸体是从弄堂68号房屋附近被移送到北四川路延伸段的日本海军医院的。当局安排了一名英国医生在场见证验尸，并邀请高恩利特医生前往。他补充说，他曾带这位医生去医院，后来又把他带了回来。

难民的故事
另一名证人是马克斯·科普斯坦（Max Kopstein），20岁，德籍犹太难民，他是涉及妓院老板过失杀人案的三名当事人之一。他通过翻译向法庭陈述，他与被告一起工作，但不在公共卫生部门任职。9月8日晚，他与李先生（Mr. Li，一名与被告在同一办公室工作的华人）一起在百老汇路的蜂鸟咖啡馆（Cafe Colibri）。当他们在该咖啡馆时，被告进来并与他们会合。他们在那里喝了几杯酒，随后又在虹口巡捕房的食堂喝了一些。另一名英国人加入了他们。食堂关闭后，他们乘车前往百老汇路，并在几家不同的咖啡馆继续饮酒。那名英国人离开后，莫里斯、李和证人沿着贝加尔路（Baikal Road）行走。

“我们进入了右边的一条弄堂，”证人叙述道，并补充说由于他们喝醉了，他记不清弄堂的确切位置。华人李某指出一扇门，有人打开了门，他们都走了进去。“里面什么也没发生，”证人说，“我们转身又走了出来。那地方是一家妓院，里面有几个女孩。我看到一名华籍男子正在扫地。我们在屋里时，没有人碰他。

不超过五拳
“我先出来，等待莫里斯和李。我转过身，看到莫里斯打了那个正在扫地的华人。我想在华人倒地之前，挨的拳头不超过五下。我说不上他是因被击打还是因绊倒而倒地的。”当被问及是否注意到弄堂里有其他人时，证人回答说，他注意到一个带着摊位的华人小贩，但没有其他人。“在那名华人被打倒后，我们走开了，穿过贝加尔路进入对面的弄堂。在韦赛德路（Wayside Road）我们分开了，莫里斯……

巡捕房警长
“我们看到那名华人躺在弄堂入口约100码处的巷道中间。他的头朝南。我对莫里斯说，我们最好去韦赛德巡捕房，但当我们试图离开时，被两名日本士兵拦住。我告诉他们我是警察，随即前往韦赛德巡捕房，并带着两名日本巡长和一名华籍侦探返回。尸体在68号房屋的后门附近。华人群众说莫里斯杀死了死者。莫里斯解释说，他打了那名华人三拳，随后那人便瘫倒了。”

昨天的最后一位证人是工务局地政处的托里·W·R·威尔逊先生（Mr. Torry W. R. Wilson）。他作证说，显示弄堂内所有房屋的贝加尔路74号弄堂平面图，以及取自该地区市政道路地图的周边道路平面图，均是在警务处的要求下，在他的监督下制作的。案件将于周五上午10点继续审理。

More Evidence
Is Heard In
Morris Case

Doctor Establishes
Cause Of Dead
Man's Demise

The prosecution in the case of manslaughter in which Mr. J. D. Morris of the Shanghai Public Health Department is accused of complicity in the death of a Chinese male as the result of a fight on the night of September 8, continued with the examination of witnesses in the British Police Court yesterday. All evidence with one exception was circumstantial. Witnesses at the proceedings held before Mr. C. H. Haines, registrar, yesterday were all foreigners.

The fact was established that the dead Chinese had been suffering from a disease and died as the result of a rupture to the main artery. Almost any unusual physical exertion would have served to break the unnaturally thin walls of the blood vessel. The only eye-witness present in court, Mr. Max Kopstein, a friend who accompanied Mr. Morris that night prefaced his testimony with the statement that he had been "really too drunk" the night of the brawl to remember what took place and later, under close examination, gave a detailed story of what he saw.

Returns To Scene

He also increased the public's estimation of the accused when he told the court that Mr. Morris had returned to the scene of the fight in order to help a friend, Mr. Lee, who had fallen prey to a Chinese mob.

Dr. E. G. Gauntlett, who was first witness on the stand yesterday said he had at the request of the Shanghai Municipal Police, on September 9, witnessed the autopsy by two Japanese naval medical doctors of a middle-aged Chinese who suffered from no visible wounds but a facial abrasion and a couple of missing teeth. On opening the right side, however, it was found full of blood. The main artery which had ruptured causing this haemorrhage was the diameter of two fists where normally it should not be more than an inch and a half across. It had been abnormal for at least six months, he said, and the man would not have had many more months to live except as an absolute invalid. It was the largest swelling of the kind he had ever seen, he said, and almost any unusual strain such as taking part in a fight might cause the sudden rupture which is the natural termination of most cases of the kind.

莫里斯案
听取更多证据

医生确定
死者死因

上海公共卫生部的 J. D. 莫里斯先生被控在9月8日晚的一场打斗中致使一名华籍男子死亡，涉嫌过失杀人一案的检方指控，昨日在英国巡捕房法庭通过证人讯问继续进行。除一项例外，所有证据均为间接证据。昨日在书记官 C. H. 海恩斯先生主持进行的诉讼程序中，所有证人均为外国人。

事实查明，死去的华人患有疾病，死于主要动脉破裂。几乎任何不寻常的体力消耗都足以撕裂血管异常薄的壁。法庭上唯一的目击证人马克斯·科普斯坦先生，是当晚陪同莫里斯先生的一位朋友，他在作证前声明，斗殴当晚他“实在醉得太厉害”，记不起发生了什么，随后在严密讯问下，详细讲述了他所看到的情况。

返回现场

他还提高了公众对被告的评价，因为他告诉法庭，莫里斯先生为了帮助沦为华人暴民受害者的朋友李先生，曾返回打斗现场。

昨天首位出庭作证的 E. G. 高恩利特医生说，应上海公共租界工部局警务处的要求，他于9月9日见证了两名日本海军军医对一名中年华人的验尸过程，该华人身上没有可见伤口，只有面部擦伤和缺失几颗牙齿。然而，打开右侧胸腔后，发现里面充满血液。导致这种出血的破裂主要动脉，其直径有两个拳头那么大，而正常情况下不应超过一英寸半。他说，这种情况至少已存在六个月，此人除非完全成为病残者，否则余命不长。他说，这是他见过的同类肿胀中最大的，几乎任何不寻常的紧张状态，如参与打斗，都可能导致突然破裂，而这通常是此类病例的自然终结。

Probationary Sergeant Edward
Meyar of the S.M.P., then testified
that he was proceeding down Way-
side road in a private car at about
2.30 a.m. on the day of the fatal

The sergeant then proceeded to

yards from Baikal road. Witness
then told Mr. Morris they should
go to a police station but when
they started to leave they were
prevented from doing so by two

told them to wait and he went
to the station where he got two
Japanese and a Chinese policemen.
On a further question witness

Kopstein Describes Events
Mr. Max Kopstein, who describ-
ed himself as a helper of accused
but not attached to the Public
Health Department, then told of
how the trio: accused, a Chinese
named Mr. Lee, and himself had
spent the evening going from one
cafe to another drinking at each
and finally ending up on Baikal

ber 9. There they turned down a
lane and Mr. Lee knocked on a
door which they entered. Inside
they spoke shortly with a man who
was sweeping the floor, subsequent-

the owner not more than five

The trio then left the alley and

too well when Sergeant Meyar
arrived.

which the three had left lying
near the door of house No. 38, it
had been moved across the alley.

day at 10 a.m.

工部局巡长作证
工部局（S.M.P.）见习巡长爱德华·梅亚尔（Edward Meyar）随后作证称，在发生致命事件的当天凌晨约2点30分，他正驾驶一辆私家车沿韦赛德路（Wayside road）行驶，途经贝加尔路（Baikal Road），即据称那名中国人死亡的地方。由于当时有一大群人在一个弄堂入口处聚集喧闹，他便上前查看，发现他认识的莫里斯先生（Mr. Morris）正被暴民拉扯。科普斯坦先生（Mr. Kopstein）也在场。经询问，莫里斯先生告诉证人他卷入了一场斗殴。暴民高喊着：“他杀了他。”

随后，该巡长前往位于距离贝加尔路约105码的弄堂中央的那名中国人的尸体处。证人随即告诉莫里斯先生他们应该去警察局，但当他们准备离开时，两名日本士兵阻止了他们。证人于是让他们等待，自己前往警局，带回了两名日本巡捕和一名中国巡捕。在进一步讯问下，证人回答说，当他询问莫里斯先生发生了什么事时，得到的回答是：“我打了他三拳，他就倒下了。”

科普斯坦描述事件经过
马克斯·科普斯坦先生（Mr. Max Kopstein）自称是被告的助手，但并不隶属于公共卫生处，他随后讲述了三人——被告、一名姓李的中国人以及他自己——如何在9月9日凌晨的几个小时内，从一家咖啡馆转到另一家咖啡馆饮酒，最后来到贝加尔路。在那里，他们转入一条弄堂，李先生敲开了一扇门并进入屋内。在里面，他们与一名正在扫地的男子简短交谈，该男子后来被确认为房主，随后便离开了房子。房东跟了出来，随之发生争执，证人说他看到被告击打房东不超过五次。随后该男子要么踉跄了一下，要么摔倒在地；证人对此并不清楚。

随后三人离开弄堂并很快分开，被告独自回家。接着，科普斯坦先生建议他和李先生返回斗殴现场，以便在可能的情况下帮助房东。他们照做了，但李先生遭到已聚集的人群的攻击。证人随即跑去寻求帮助，找到了被告，并在告知他李先生遇到麻烦后，说服他返回。当他们返回时，被告也遭到攻击，局势看起来不太妙，这时梅亚尔巡长赶到了。

关于那三人留在38号房屋门口附近的尸体位置，它已被移至弄堂对面。听证会休庭至周五上午10点。

Then the proprietor of the house

clearly."

昨日，在英国警察法庭，由英国驻华法院书记官 C. H. Haines 先生主持，继续对工部局公共卫生处舟山路分部雇员、36岁的英国人约翰·达德利·莫里斯（John Dudley Morris）进行过失杀人指控的初步审讯。9月9日凌晨，在一名叫丁树成（Ting Shucheng）的男子据称在其家中发生斗殴后死亡之后，莫里斯与一名德籍犹太难民及一名中国人被日本海军陆战队当局拘留。

他随后被移交给上海公共租界工部局警务处，但该德籍犹太难民和那名据称名为李延民（Li Yen-min）的中国人仍由日本当局羁押。莫里斯在接受讯问后，被工部局警务处当局告诫并以过失杀人罪起诉。

昨日传唤的第一位证人是王阿三（Wang Ah-san），目前失业，居住在杨树浦路56号74弄（清阳里）。在回答控方律师 G. H. Wright 先生的提问时，他说9月8日他在一个弄堂口吃面条。在此之前，他一直在杨树浦路74号70号打麻雀牌（麻将），该房屋紧邻68号。凌晨约2点15分，他结束牌局出去买面条。

翻译受到质疑

此时，辩方律师 H. A. Reeks 先生对译员的翻译提出质疑，Wright 先生惊呼：“这不可能。” Reeks 先生表示：“我只是想帮你。” 书记官对 Reeks 先生说：“如果你想质疑这位译员，为什么不聘请一位宣誓过的译员以便核查，然后我们再听你的意见？”

证人继续作证说，小贩的摊位正好在68号对面。当他在摊位吃面时，他看到两名外国人和一名中国人从贝加尔路（北端）进入弄堂后敲击68号的门。他们进入了房子，但他不知道里面发生了什么。

随后，房主被推了出来，一名外国人（较高的一位）袭击了他。证人补充说，房主手里拿着一把扫帚，当他的胸部和下巴被握紧的拳头击打时，他喊道：“先生，谢谢，我是个伙计。” 与两名外国人在一起的那名中国人随后辱骂他，同一名外国人更猛烈地殴打他。此时证人被问及是否能认出那名外国人，他回答说：“天很黑，我看不太清楚。”

SHANGHAI TIMES,

SEP 22 . 39

Witnesses Say Morris Hit
Deceased With Fists

Two Eye-Witness Accounts Of Struggle; Chinese
Shouts “I Will Kill You In Ten Minutes”;
Other Foreigner Did Not Fight

The preliminary examination of Mr. John Dudley Morris, of the S.M.C., Public Health Department, on a complaint of manslaughter was continued in the British Police Court yesterday morning before the Registrar, Mr. C. H. Haines, when two more Chinese witnesses gave evidence. They were an unemployed Chinese and a food hawker, who stated that they saw the accused striking the deceased with his fists until the latter fell down.

One of the witnesses claimed that he heard the Chinese member of the trio shout, “I will kill you in ten minutes.” He called the Japanese soldiers, and when they returned they found the victim of the assault lying dead in the lane. Mr. G. H. Wright appeared for the S.M.P., and Mr. H A. Reeks for the accused.

The first witness to take the stand yesterday was an unemployed Chinese named Wang Ah-san of House No. 56, Lane 74, Baikal Road. He said that he had been playing mahjongg in House No. 70, which is next door to No. 68, the brothel owned by the deceased. “At about 2.15 in the night, I left the house to buy noodles from a stall, which was just opposite the house on the other side of the alleyway,” he added. As I was eating noodles, I saw the two foreigners and the Chinese enter House 68. They had come from Baikal Road.”

Struck With Fists

“About 10 minutes later the proprietor of House 68 was pushed out into the lane. He was holding a broom. Then the taller foreigner beat him with clenched fists. He struck him mostly on the chest and also on the chin. The proprietor said ‘Thank you, mister, thank you. I am an employee,’ while he was being struck. The Chinese then hurled abuse at the deceased and the foreigner beat him more severely. The Chinese shouted ‘I will kill you in 10 minutes’ and started to take off his jacket in order to beat the proprietor. He also said that they had come from the Municipal Council.”

The witness stated that he could not see very clearly, but could identify the foreigner, and pointed to the accused in the dock. Continuing with his story he told the Registrar that the three men then left and went away towards Baikal Road, leaving the proprietor lying in the alleyway groaning. The witness said that the deceased was lying on the opposite corner of the lane between Houses 53 and 56. “I saw the man was dying, and so I went to report to the Police Station, but I was stopped by a Japanese soldier opposite Wayside Wharf and asked what was the matter.

“I replied that a man had been beaten to death at Tsing Yang li, the Chinese name for Lane 74. The Japanese soldier came back with me to the lane and arrested the two foreigners and the Chinese. There was plenty of talk, and then more Japanese soldiers came along. The three visitors were taken into House 56, the house where I live, while the proprietor was still lying on the ground.” The witness stated that he did not know the name of the noodles seller. Mr. H. A. Reeks reserved his cross-examination.

Noodles Seller’s Story

Wei Yue-sing, the food hawker, next took the stand. He said he sold noodles and beef for a living from his portable stall. On the night of September 8, he was in the lane called Tsing Yang Li and he identified the first witness as a customer who came to buy noodles that night after 2 o’clock. The first time he noticed the three visitors, they were fighting “One foreigner was beating the proprietor a short distance from my stall,” he told the court. “I saw only one foreigner fighting, but I cannot identify him. He beat the deceased with his fists, and then the proprietor fell down right beside my stall. I packed up my stall and went away. I did not see anyone touch the deceased while he was lying on the ground, nor did I see the Chinese fight the proprietor”

Again Mr. Reeks reserved his cross-examination, and the hearing was adjourned until Monday, September 25, at 10 a.m.

证人称莫里斯用拳头
击打死者

两起目击者对争斗的描述；中国人喊叫“十分钟内我要杀了你”；
另一名外国人未参与打斗

昨日早晨，在英国警察法庭，由书记官 C. H. Haines 先生主持，继续对工部局公共卫生处的约翰·达德利·莫里斯先生进行过失杀人指控的初步审讯，期间又有两名中国证人出庭作证。他们是一名失业中国人和一名食品小贩，均表示看到被告用拳头击打死者，直至后者倒地。

其中一名证人声称，他听到三人中的那名中国人大喊：“十分钟内我要杀了你。”他叫来了日本士兵，当他们返回时，发现袭击受害者已死在弄堂里。G. H. Wright 先生代表工部局警务处出庭，H. A. Reeks 先生代表被告出庭。

昨日第一位出庭的证人是一名失业中国人，名叫王阿三，住在贝加尔路74弄56号。他说他曾在70号打麻将，70号紧邻68号，即死者拥有的妓院。“夜里大约2点15分，我离开房子去对面的弄堂另一边的小摊买面条，”他补充道。“当我吃面条时，我看到两名外国人和一名中国人进入68号。他们是从贝加尔路来的。”

用拳头击打

“大约10分钟后，68号的房主被推到了弄堂里。他手里拿着一把扫帚。然后那个较高的外国人用握紧的拳头殴打他。主要击打他的胸部，也打了他的下巴。房主在挨打时说‘谢谢你，先生，谢谢。我是个伙计’。随后那名中国人辱骂死者，而那名外国人更猛烈地殴打他。那名中国人大喊‘十分钟内我要杀了你’，并开始脱下夹克以殴打房主。他还说他们来自工部局。”

证人表示他看不太清楚，但能认出那名外国人，并指认了被告席上的被告。他继续向书记官讲述，随后这三名男子离开，朝贝加尔路方向走去，留下房主躺在弄堂里呻吟。证人说，死者躺在弄堂对面角落，介于53号和56号房屋之间。“我看到那人快死了，所以我去警察局报案，但在韦赛德码头（Wayside Wharf）对面被一名日本士兵拦住，问我出了什么事。

“我回答说，有人在清阳里（即74弄的中文名称）被打死了。日本士兵随我回到弄堂，逮捕了两名外国人和那名中国人。现场议论纷纷，随后又来了更多的日本士兵。这三名访客被带入56号房屋，即我居住的房子，而房主仍躺在地上。”证人表示他不知道卖面条者的名字。H. A. Reeks 先生保留交叉质询的权利。

卖面者的陈述

食品小贩魏岳生（Wei Yue-sing）随后出庭。他说他靠流动摊位卖面条和牛肉为生。9月8日晚，他在名为清阳里的弄堂里，他指认第一位证人是当晚2点后前来买面条的顾客。他第一次注意到这三名访客时，他们正在打斗。“一名外国人在离我摊位不远的地方殴打房主，”他告诉法庭。“我只看到一名外国人在打斗，但我无法辨认出他是谁。他用拳头殴打死者，然后房主就倒在我的摊位旁边。我收拾好摊位就离开了。我没有看到任何人在死者躺在地上时触碰他，也没有看到那名中国人与房主打斗。”

Reeks 先生再次保留交叉质询的权利，听证会休庭至9月25日星期一上午10点。
